Andy Burnham has announced the comeback of the council house as he unveiled a £10bn package to build 70,000 new homes in England.

Building thousands of new council houses was one of his “day one’ priorities when taking over from Sir Keir Starmer in July, when he warned that “no child should be raised in a hostel room and no family should wait 10 years for a front door of their own”.

It marks the first major spending announcement of the Burnham government – although the cash comes from a £39bn fund agreed by Sir Keir and ex-chancellor Rachel Reeves in the 2025 spending review.

It builds on the government’s commitment to deliver 1.5 million homes this parliament, including the biggest boost to council, social and affordable housing in a generation – amid concerns the target will be missed. It also comes as the prime minister has made ending rough sleeping a major priority.

The announcement will see councils across England receive the cash to build thousands of new homes with new powers to get building accelerated and make decisions in their areas.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham is unveiling a council house building package ( AFP/Getty )

“I have said from my first day in this job that everything starts with a good home,” said the prime minister, who has also pushed a decentralisation policy.

“Nearly £10bn will go to councils and housing associations to build genuinely affordable homes, most of them for social rent, in the places where families are waiting longest.

“Councils built this country out of a housing crisis once before. Backed properly, and trusted to get on with it, they will do it again.”

The move is meant to be the start of a reversal of the social housing crisis, which has its origins in Margaret Thatcher’s mass sell-off of council houses to occupants in the 1980s.

Failure to replace sold-off stock, along with added bureaucracy around building new homes, has left some areas with waiting lists as long as 50 years.

The announcement comes just 24 hours after Reform UK revealed their plans to build 50,000 social-housing homes a year but prioritising married people, military veterans and only making them available to people born in the UK.

Reform deputy leader Richard Tice, who was a property entrepreneur, admitted the failure to replace council housing stocks after the Thatcher sell-off had been “a mistake”.

But Tory shadow housing secretary Sir James Cleverly claimed that Mr Burnham’s package was “a sleight of hand” and warned that it is “yet another unfunded spending commitment”.

He said: “The small print shows homes won’t have to be delivered until 2039. And the funding has been backloaded to fall outside the Spending Review and this Parliament, meaning Andy Burnham will never have to pay for it. Instead, it'll be another cheque written by Labour PM and left for future generations to cover.

“Fewer homes will be delivered than previous programmes in this Parliament as social rent is more expensive. Labour have scaled back their affordable housing programme and expect us to thank them for it.”

According to the government around a fifth of the funds, £2 million, will go to London to build thousands of homes.

open image in gallery Angela Rayner (right) and Andy Burnham have also made tackling homelessness a priority ( Getty )

Greater Manchester, where Mr Burnham was until recently mayor, gets the second highest allocation with £529m for 4,400 homes.

The West Midlands will get £409m for 3,200 homes; the North East £445m for 3,400 homes; West Yorkshire £441m for 4,000 homes; Liverpool £380m for 3,100 homes; and South Yorkshire £249m for 2,200 homes.

Housing secretary Angela Rayner said: “Families can’t be left raising children without a place to call home, and none of us should spend years waiting for somewhere safe and affordable to live.

“I know how important fixing this is – because I’ve been there. A safe and secure home was the foundation for a better life – I couldn’t have got to where I have today without it.”

The allocation is only the first stage of a 10-year programme. More than £16bn remains to be allocated outside London in what is intended to be the largest expansion of council housing in decades.

London mayor Sir Sadiq Khan said: “Tackling the housing crisis is one of my top priorities and I’m doing everything I can to deliver more affordable homes that Londoners desperately need. We’ve built record numbers of council homes in London, but the number of families and children without a permanent home stuck on housing waiting lists is still unacceptable. I want to work with this new government to deliver a step change in how many council homes we can deliver across the capital.

“Thousands of Londoners will benefit from this new wave of new social and affordable homes, which will help people out of temporary accommodation and provide good, affordable homes to live in for the long-term, as we build a fairer, better London for everyone.”

Housing associations and other providers will continue to play a vital role in delivering the social and affordable homes the country needs.

Alongside councils, they will be central to delivering the government’s ambition to increase housebuilding and expand access to genuinely affordable homes.

Kate Henderson, chief executive of the National Housing Federation, said: “It is hugely welcome to see this much-anticipated funding confirmed, something we have been calling for to kickstart construction on tens of thousands of desperately needed new social homes.

“This is a major vote of confidence in not-for-profit housing associations and in the vital and distinct role they play in this country, as organisations that work for the long-term benefit of their communities.”

Gavin Smart, chief executive at the Chartered Institute of Housing, said: “We welcome the strong focus on homes for social rent and the ambition for council housebuilding, and the recognition of the vital role that councils, housing associations and other providers will play in delivering the next generation of genuinely affordable homes. If delivered at pace, this investment has the potential to reduce homelessness, ease pressure on temporary accommodation and help more people access a safe, secure and affordable home.”

News.title: This summer’s wildfire epidemic is one of the worst in decades – so why are deaths so low?
News.content:
Wildfires in Britain and Europe this year are among the worst in decades, yet direct deaths are at some of the lowest levels, according to a Telegraph analysis.

As of early August, 505,683 hectares of land have burned across Europe, forcing the evacuation of more than 360,000 people as uncontrollable flames reach major cities, towns, and villages.

The problem is global – in the US, Nevada declared a state of emergency over the weekend after a wildfire caused more than 42,000 people to evacuate their homes.

But what sets 2026 apart isn’t just the vast areas of land burned, but how few deaths have been caused by the fires.

This summer, just 14 people are reported to have died in European wildfires, the vast majority in a single blaze in Almería, southern Spain.

By comparison, more than 130 people were killed in the summer of 2017 – a toll driven largely by the Pedrógão Grande disaster in Portugal, where more than 60 people died on a single stretch of road.

In 2018, at least 100 others died in a single afternoon in the Mati disaster near Athens, despite total hectares burned that year being roughly a third of current levels.

Since the modern phenomenon of summer wildfires exploded in Europe a decade ago, the direct death toll has broadly trended downward, as the chart below shows.

News.title: Swine flu outbreak in Delhi swamps clinics and hospitals
News.content:
India is battling a surge in H1N1 flu infections, prompting the federal health ministry to step up surveillance and hospital preparedness.

The national capital New Delhi has recorded 1,777 cases this year, almost eight times the number (229) reported during the same period in 2025.

Dr Randeep Guleria, a senior pulmonologist and director of Medanta Medical School, Gurugram, says the H1N1 cases are much higher than reported.

“It’s quite likely that the reported numbers are an underestimate because they depend on how many people are tested,” Guleria said. “If you speak to patients admitted to hospital who test positive for H1N1, you often find that other members of their family have similar symptoms, although they have not been tested.”

“There is a surge and we are seeing a lot of patients. We are testing only those who come to hospital and are more seriously ill,” Guleria said.

H1N1, commonly known as swine flu, is a subtype of influenza A. It is a contagious respiratory infection that can cause fever and cough and in severe cases it can lead to pneumonia and respiratory failure.

Officials at the Indian Council of Medical Research said the rise did not mean the emergence of a new strain of the virus.

The surge comes during India’s rainy season, when seasonal influenza and other respiratory infections typically increase.

Doctors in Delhi say they are seeing more patients with high fevers, persistent coughs and flu-like symptoms, although most cases remain mild.

The H1N1 cases have been reported beyond New Delhi. The metro cities like Mumbai, Chennai and Bangaluru have reported a high number of cases, although the pattern is not uniform across the country.

Doctors in Bangaluru have reported more influenza A infections among children, with some developing pneumonia and respiratory distress.

India’s health minister JP Nadda said there was a need for continued vigilance and robust surveillance. He has asked officials to monitor unusual increases and clusters of cases and ensure hospitals could respond quickly.

“Swine flu (H1N1) can show up through symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue… If you experience these symptoms, seek medical advice at your nearest healthcare centre,” the health ministry said on X.

Delhi’s health minister, Pankaj Kumar Singh, said the capital had enough beds, doctors, medicines and medical equipment to manage the increase. “Delhi is fully prepared to deal with the present health situation,” Singh said.

India has had several waves of H1N1 since the virus emerged globally in 2009.

The infection, commonly called swine flu, became a recurring seasonal respiratory illness after the 2009 pandemic rather than disappearing from circulation.

India recorded 3,320 H1N1 cases and 14 deaths in 2025, according to Ministry of Health data.

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Frustrated Russell fails to make up ground as Norris wins incident-packed Dutch GP
News.content:
George Russell had another frustrating Sunday as the Dutch Grand Prix weekend slipped by with him failing to reduce his deficit to leader Kimi Antonelli. In a thrilling finale to the 72-lap race at the Dutch seaside, Lando Norris took his second victory in a row with two bold overtakes in one lap.

Yet compatriot Russell was irritated by Mercedes team orders for him to let Antonelli through into second place in the closing stages. It was a decision he believed risked a double podium for the team and threatened to put him even further behind his team-mate in the standings, with two charging Ferraris close behind. It was a race that, once again, fell away, despite Russell doing little wrong.

“Is he [Antonelli] fighting for the win or is he planning to catch Norris?” he asked, when the McLaren driver was 11 seconds down the road – the margin he would win by. “Yeah – we just lost a double podium here, mate,” was his response after moving aside.

Whilst Norris, who lost his lead from pole to Antonelli on the first lap, sealed the victory with two superb overtakes on lap 54 – first the Italian and then Lewis Hamilton – Russell had to mount a stout defence from Hamilton to secure third. It was against the odds, as both Ferraris, like Antonelli, were on fresh rubber after pitting under a late virtual safety car. Like Russell, Hamilton was critical of his team for their strategy choices.

Russell’s first podium finish since Silverstone – with his sprint victory on Saturday – means he at least retakes second place in the championship from Hamilton, but trails Antonelli by the same 59 point-gap he had after Hungary. That is despite him looking the faster and more comfortable Mercedes driver on Friday and Saturday.

News.title: Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win
News.content:
Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

News.title: How to spend a weekend in Lake Garda
News.content:
Lake Garda’s glittering wind-swept waters have long attracted poets, artists, writers and politicians, from DH Lawrence to Wolfgang Goethe – not least Mussolini, who ran the Italian Socialist Republic from the lakefront town of Salò on the western shore.

Fringed by the Dolomites to the north, Italy’s largest lake is Mediterranean both in feel and in flavour, with a mild, temperate climate and a decidedly slow pace of life. Hills are carpeted in olive trees and vineyards, while citrus groves are thick with plump, juicy lemons. In lakefront villages, restaurant tables spill out onto pretty waterfront squares, while boats zip across glimmering waters.

The lower basin is punctuated with sandy coves and gentle rolling hills, while travelling north, the lake takes on a new appearance, with hills replaced by sheer jagged cliffs that plunge into the waters. The northern shore is swept by mountain winds that create the perfect conditions for watersports, with windsailing, kitesurfing, and flyboarding making this a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts.

News.title: How to spend a perfect weekend in Lake Como
News.content:
An hour drive north of Milan, Lake Como is the most glamorous of Italy’s lakes, hemmed in by the snow-capped Alps with picture-perfect villages on the water. Milanesi pop here for the day for a breath of fresh air and to soak up the fabulous vistas, while international visitors – the Clooneys, the Kennedys – have long been drawn by the grand lakefront hotels and the elegant mahogany Riva boats that zip along the lake’s deep blue waters.

Smart hotels and expensive boats aside, Lake Como is rich in culture, with opulent villas that once belonged to artists, writers, opera singers and explorers. Pliny the Elder, author of the first encyclopaedia, was born here, while 19th-century soprano Giuditta Pasta is known to have entertained composers Bellini and Donizetti in her lakefront residence on the eastern shore.

Though famous spots such as pretty Bellagio still pull in the majority of visitors, the lake has retained its authenticity, with plenty of sleepy fishing villages, such as Laglio, Torno and Nesso, home to rustic, family-run trattorias serving up traditional hearty fare, including risotto al pesce persico (risotto with perch).

Sports.title: Ruben Dias’ romance with model exposed after she shares videos from Man City star’s BED months after Maya Jama split
Sports.content:

PALLY WITH VALLY Ruben Dias’ romance with model exposed after she shares videos from Man City star’s BED months after Maya Jama split

RUBEN Dias’ new romance with a model has been rumbled after she posted videos from his BED.

The Manchester City defender invited Valentina Best, known as Vally, to stay the night at the home he shared with ex Maya Jama until April.



Fans recognised the bedroom decor from Maya’s previous shots and the road outside the modern £4million mansion from a selfie.

The four-bed home’s kitchen and gym also featured — matching snaps in the home’s listing when it was a prize in an Omaze charity draw.



Ruben, 29, and Love Island host Maya, 31, bought the home from the winner just before Christmas last year, but broke up in April.

The final clue for online sleuths was seeing a snap showing the nearby Costa Coffee shop in Alderley Edge, Cheshire.



Dias was first linked to German Vally, 28, in 2024.

She has 170,000 followers online and shares snaps as she travels the world.



The Sun revealed Dias and Maya’s split after sources said the couple had “reached a crossroads” ahead of a hectic summer.

Portuguese Ruben was playing in the World Cup while Maya was facing a busy filming schedule.

Last month Dias told magazine Esquire Portugal he still hoped to find a serious relationship “just like anyone else”.

Sports.title: Chelsea player ratings: Joao Pedro makes mockery of No9 curse as Sanchez shows new keeper needed after win over Fulham
Sports.content:
Chelsea might be a little cold, after all.

Joao Pedro got Chelsea‘s season off to the perfect start after just 31 seconds with a delightful chip over Bernd Leno, having been set up by Cole Palmer in a 3-2 win at Craven Cottage.



But with the lead in their hands, Chelsea showed the same signals of distress that we saw under Enzo Maresca, Liam Rosenior and Calum McFarlane – a lack of discipline and too many silly mistakes.

Josh King bought the scores level with a powerful effort after 23 minutes, but Robert Sanchez should have done better to stop it.



Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

With Chelsea in need of a goal before half-time to calm things down, enter stage left, Morgan Rogers.

Maxence Lacroix could have got a nose bleed with how high up the pitch he found himself, but instead weaved his way into the box and delivered the ball across the box for Rogers to finish.

With Pedro and Rogers on the scoresheet, it was time for Palmer to join in the action.

Pedro controlled the ball brilliantly and held it up just as well before laying the ball off to his teammate who slotted through Leno’s legs to give the Blues breathing room and wrap up the win despite another Fulham goal from Gonzalo Garcia.

This is how SunSport Chelsea reporter Lloyd Canfield rated the players…

ROBERT SANCHEZ – 2

Not again, Rob. Please. Don’t give Chelsea fans another season of this.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Didn’t look assured at the back for the Blues, with some questionable passes out from the back, before a really poor bit of shot stopping for Josh King’s equaliser.

His role in Fulham’s second goal was not so disastrous, but still not good enough as he palmed the ball out to Gonzalo Garcia to score a goal which got Fulham back into the game again.

A few routine catches and saves is not good enough, Chelsea need a new goalkeeper in order to not undermine an otherwise good transfer window.

JOSH ACHEAMPONG – 8

Made several crucial blocks and clearances, particularly with the score at 1-1 to keep the Blues in the game.

Was probably Chelsea’s best actual defender in the back three tonight, with the other two struggling a little in this system – one of his best performances in a Blue shirt and he should be rewarded with more minutes.



MAXENCE LACROIX – 7

His first competitive game for Chelsea saw him look a little bit unsure of himself on the ball to start with, but he certainly sorted those issues out before half-time with a wonderful assist for Morgan Rogers first Premier League goal in Chelsea blue.

Really grew as the game went on.

LEVI COLWILL – 3

Levi Colwill was perhaps a little fortunate not to be sent off in the opening ten minutes after a poorly timed tackle on Oscar Bobb after mis-controlling a pass from his teammate.

He’s usually such a consistent performer, but tonight really wasn’t his night, and there was a case to be made for him being sent off on a second occasion in the first half too.



He was caught out of position for Fulham’s second goal too, and just looked out of sorts from the off in this game.

MALO GUSTO – 4

The less threatening of Chelsea’s wingbacks, he was far from convincing despite some decent moments.

It was quite a quiet day for the Frenchman, but in his role you want someone loud who is making things happen, and Blues fans will be excited to see Marco Palestra or even Pedro Neto there instead.

JORREL HATO – 6

Was better than Gusto, particularly going forwards, but had some shaky moments defensively, it’s hard to see where he fits in this Chelsea team long term, as he would ideally be the left sided player in a back three, where Levi Colwill plays.

A real mixed bag from the Dutchman.



ROMEO LAVIA – 6

The role of replacing Moises Caicedo is not an easy one to fill.

Got booked after 11 minutes for a bad tackle on Calvin Bassey who was breaking out from the back for Fulham – and walked the tightrope for the rest of the game quite well.

Almost put Chelsea 2-1 up in the first half when his close range effort following a set-piece was denied by Bernd Leno.

REECE JAMES – 6

Was far from the standout performer, but quietly quite good, the captain.



Influences the game in an attacking and defensive dynamic when he is at his best, and wasn’t quite there today, but still showed his quality and stepped up in midfield with Caicedo out and Enzo Fernandez on the bench.

COLE PALMER – 9

Cole Palmer is back.

With so much conversation about Palmer over the summer, an assist just 31 seconds into the new season will do the Chelsea number 10 a world of good.

He was full of confidence after the opening goal, and looked desperate for one of his own, although he was perhaps a little too greedy at times – a lesson he seemed to learn when he was also involved in Chelsea’s second.

Trying too hard can sometimes be the enemy of progress, but not today for ice-cold Cole, whose consistent and overwhelming effort saw him sprint past Joao Pedro and claim a goal of his own in the second half.



MORGAN ROGERS – 7

The new £117million man bagged on his first competitive Chelsea start after some brilliant work from Lacroix, and might have to pay a fee to Cole Palmer for using his trademarked celebration in the aftermath.

He was caught off guard defensively for Josh King’s equaliser, but all was forgiven when he found the back of the net 18 minutes later.

JOAO PEDRO – 9

Number nine curse who?

It took just 31 seconds for Joao Pedro to get off the mark this season, with a delightful chip over the goalkeeper after latching onto Cole Palmer’s through ball.



His assist for Chelsea’s third, as he repaid the favour to Cole Palmer, was full of just as much quality.

A great touch, a great run and a great lay-off showed why he is turning into such a complete number nine.

He thought he had a second late on, but for the offside flag.

SUBS:

ENZO FERNANDEZ (ROMEO LAVIA, 65) – 5

Kept things ticking nicely when he came on, but was far from exhilarating.



He was booed by anyone in the stadium not supporting Chelsea, but that reaction didn’t seem to bother him too much.

PEP CHAVARRIA (JORREL HATO, 65) – 6

Was solid after replacing Hato on the left for Chelsea, with the Blues seeming a little more assured, although the missed Hato’s attacking presence to a degree.

PEDRO NETO (MALO GUSTO, 76) – 5

Didn’t have much time to make a big impact, but did what was required of him in working hard defensively out wide.

GEOVANY QUENDA (MORGAN ROGERS, 83) – 6

An exciting double change saw he and Estevao introduced together, as supposedly the next generation of exciting Chelsea talents in attack, replacing Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He showed flashes of pace and a willingness to defend, and would have been involved in a late Joao Pedro goal, but for the offside flag.



ESTEVAO (COLE PALMER, 83) – N/A

Similarly to Quenda, he didn’t have much time to make an impact, but always looks good on the ball and gets fans up for it.

Sports.title: Fulham 2 Chelsea 3: Cole Palmer back to his best as he, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers win thriller at Craven Cottage
Sports.content:
CHELSEA’S front three decided a brilliant game with a performance to send shivers down the spines of their rivals.

But Blues goalkeeper Robert Sanchez had the same effect on his own supporters as another gaffe-filled display helped Fulham play a full part in a classic derby.



There is rarely a dull moment on or off the field at Stamford Bridge.

And if this game is anything to go by, Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea are going to be a brilliant watch for neutrals this season – for good reasons and bad.



In Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and new signing Morgan Rogers, Alonso has potentially the best attacking unit in the Premier League.

All three scored, Pedro after 31 seconds to give the new manager a dream start.

But Sanchez was at fault for Josh King’s equaliser and for the Gonzalo Garcia goal which made it 3-2 after Rogers and Palmer had found the net either side of half-time.

Just like last season under two permanent managers and one interim boss, Chelsea looked incapable of controlling a game.

But unlike so many matches in the chaotic 2025-26 campaign, the Blues were able to hold on for victory.

Chelsea arrived with bad memories of their last visit to Craven Cottage.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Days after the departure of boss Enzo Maresca in January, the Blues had Marc Cucurella sent off in a 2-1 defeat.

As the rain lashed down, the Blues fans aimed X-rated chants at club supremo Behdad Eghbali, who was sitting next to new head coach Liam Rosenior.

Those were dark omens for a sunny summer evening.

When it emerged Moises Caicedo was out injured, the stage was set for a tough evening.

Yet after barely half a minute, Chelsea’s latest new era had the best possible start.



Maxence Lacroix’s clearing header reached Palmer, who helped the ball first time on to Pedro.

The Brazilian’s brilliant chipped finish over Bernd Leno was that of a man brimming with confidence.

The home crowd were understandably dumbstruck, the away fans jubilant.

Yet if they expected their team’s nerves to be settled, they were to be disappointed.

The normally reliable Levi Colwill miscontrolled a routine pass, Oscar Bobb nipped in, and the Blues defender was booked for stopping him running clear.



Romeo Lavia soon followed Colwill into the book for a hefty foul on Calvin Bassey.

Sanchez also gave notice of what was to come.

First the Chelsea ‘keeper let a backpass go out for a corner, then he made an unconvincing save from a King shot.

Although Palmer, Rogers and Pedro remained menacing and were one good pass away from extending Chelsea’s lead, the arrival of the equaliser was no surprise.

Rogers’ failure to go with his runner allowed King to execute a simple one-two with Timothy Castagne.



Sanchez’s positioning looked wrong and his limp-wristed attempt to stop the ball beating him at his near post was even worse.

Chelsea were rattled.

Josh Acheampong, playing instead of the suspended Wesley Fofana, made two crucial challenges to stop the home team going in front.

The visitors regained their composure and Pedro volleyed wide from a Palmer cross.

Leno saved comfortably from Reece James, then less so from Lavia, before Rogers restored the lead.



Palmer found Lacroix with a cute pass and the centre-back dropped his shoulder, beat Jorge Cuenca and pulled the ball back perfectly past Leno into the centre of the area.

Rogers redeemed himself for his part in the equaliser by sidefooting home.

Palmer upped the ante after the break.

After a mesmerising run which deserved a better finish, he made no mistake with his next chance.

Pedro ran from his own half and waited for Palmer to join him.



The Chelsea No10, from a narrow angle, fired through Leno’s legs.

Moments later it was almost 4-1, but Antonee Robinson stopped Rogers capitalising on Jorrel Hato’s surging run and cross.

Instead it was soon 2-3.

Colwill misjudged a cross and Sanchez could only parry Castagne’s shot straight on to the head of Garcia, who did not know much about his debut goal but cared even less.

Every drama needs a villain.



Enter Enzo Fernandez.

He and fellow Argentinian Valentin Barco had been roundly booed earlier in the evening, but Fernandez’s introduction in place of Lavia with 25 minutes to go took the abuse to new X-rated levels

But some away fans sang their player’s name, despite knowing he would love to be at Manchester City before the end of the window.

After a lull, Fulham went again, with King dragging a shot wide of Sanchez’s right-hand post.

Bassey was booked for diving in the penalty area, then Robinson raced clear of James, only to send his shot over Sanchez but wide.



The Chelsea ‘keeper kept out an effort by substitute Ryan Sessegnon and Pedro had a late effort ruled out for offside.

But the Blues are up and running, and it promises to be a fun ride.

Sports.title: Premier League’s 11,000-capacity stadium NOT READY for weekend clash as builders work round clock on new additions
Sports.content:
BOURNEMOUTH builders are working around the clock to get the revamped Vitality Stadium ready for Saturday’s home kick-off against Everton.

The Cherries announced last week their home will be open for business in

time with sections of the stadium closed.



But exclusive SunSport photos show huge lifting machinery still being

used with just five days to go before Everton head to the south coast.

Floodlights at two of the corners of the Steve Fletcher and Ted

MacDougall stands behind the goal have been moved to make way for the

new corners.



The north west and east corners, which are set to hold an extra 800 fans, will not be ready until early in the season.

When one security guard was asked last night if the stadium would be

ready for Saturday he raised his eyebrows and puffed out his cheeks.

And then he smiled: “Of course it will be ready!”

The main cark park and surrounding pathways around the stadium are

full of rubble, iron and concrete fittings that need to be cleared for

safety standards.



Extensive work has been carried out by Bournemouth to meet European

football regulations having qualified for the Europa League for the

first time in their history.

Media facilities have had to be improved for additional overseas TV

and radio commentators, reporters and photographers.

The Cherries have also revamped their hospitality suites and laid a new

pitch for the start of the new campaign.



Bournemouth’s billionaire American owner Bill Foley and the board

opted to expand their current home rather than build a new stadium

away from the site.

The Vitality Stadium will grow from roughly 11,300 seats to 20,200

when all the work has been completed by around the summer of 2027.

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers ignores Cole Palmer’s ‘bailiffs threat’ with Chelsea celebration – but pal has brilliant response
Sports.content:
MORGAN ROGERS showed he wouldn’t be intimidated by his £117m transfer fee – or his team-mate’s warning – as he scored 41 minutes into his Chelsea debut.

The England star, who joined from Aston Villa, then performed the iconic ‘ice-cold’ celebration, shared by himself and Cole Palmer.



In pre-season, Palmer had jokingly warned Rogers not to perform the celebration or risk facing “bailiffs”.

Palmer said at the end of July: “He does it. I do it. I’ve trademarked it so if he tries to do anything, he’ll have the bailiffs at his door.”



Chelsea ace Palmer has made the celebration his own over the years.

However, it was actually Rogers who performed it first.



The pair played together in the Man City academy but Rogers aired the celebration when he scored for Middlesbrough against West Brom on December 23, 2023.

And a week later, Cole Palmer performed the celebration during a 3-2 Chelsea win at Luton as a nod to his former, and future, team-mate.

But it was actually invented by Atlanta Hawks NBA star Trae Young back in 2018.

Palmer got his chance to respond in the 48th minute however, as he gave Chelsea a 3-1 lead.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Captain Reece James also jokingly joined in with the ‘cold’ celebration as Palmer got even with pal Rogers.

Chelsea took the lead away to West London rivals Fulham after just 31 seconds as Joao Pedro scored the fastest ever opening day goal.

But a howler from Robert Sanchez saw the Cottagers equalise through Josh King on 23 minutes.

Chelsea reestablished their lead on 41 minutes however, as a brilliant piece of work from fellow new signing Maxence Lacroix set up Rogers for a tap-in.

Rogers was one of England’s top performers during his fleeting appearances under Thomas Tuchel at the World Cup.



And that, following an excellent two seasons at Aston Villa, convinced Chelsea to splash out the huge nine-figure fee on the winger.

Sports.title: Fans burned and injured after fireworks thrown in shocking Dutch league match
Sports.content:
Fans burned and injured after fireworks thrown in shocking Dutch league match

Seven supporters were left with burns as well as damage to their hearing and vision after away fans let off fireworks inside the stadium midway through a match

View 2 Images Feyenoord goalkeeper Tjark Ernst narrowly avoided being hit by a firework during the disturbance (Image: Getty Images)

SC Cambuur have confirmed seven of their supporters were injured by fireworks set off from the away section during their Eredivisie home match against Feyenoord. The club from Leeuwarden state that their injuries range from burns to hearing and vision damage after a large-scale setting off of fireworks from the Kooi Stadion's south stand.

‌



Cambuur's initial statement on Sunday evening listed the number of injuries as five. An update on Monday afternoon then increased that total by two to seven.

‌



Play was paused in the 12th minute for 10 minutes due to the disruption. Feyenoord went on to win 5-2.

‌



The statement shared on Sunday evening reads: "What should have been a football party between SC Cambuur and Feyenoord was marred in the twelfth minute this afternoon by the large-scale setting off of fireworks. From the away section in the South stand, Feyenoord 'supporters' not only set off fireworks, but also fired towards the field and the surrounding stands.

"Five injured supporters are to be regretted with burns, hearing damage and eye damage as the main injuries. It goes without saying that all care and attention goes out to these injured supporters, and everyone at the club sympathises enormously.

"The match was eventually resumed after a strike of about ten minutes, and this is in line with the protocols of the KNVB and in consultation with the parties involved. It should be clear that setting off and firing fireworks is completely unacceptable and in no way belongs in a football stadium. Together with the authorities, we will do everything in our power to track down and punish the perpetrators."

‌



View 2 Images Fireworks were thrown onto the pitch and into other sections of supporters (Image: Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

They then added in an update barely 24 hours later: "Following on from the message below, we can now unfortunately report that not five, but seven supporters fell victim to the fireworks from the away section yesterday afternoon at the match between SC Cambuur and Feyenoord.

‌



"There has now been personal contact with six of these victims, and we would also like to get in touch with the seventh person to provide appropriate aftercare and to assist with advice and assistance.

"In addition, there will also be an official report from the club towards the perpetrators. The search for these people is in full swing under the leadership of Feyenoord, and in cooperation with all parties involved. A new update will follow later this week."

Feyenoord general manager Robert Eenhoorn also condemned the incident. He said: "It is of course especially terrible for a number of injured Cambuur supporters. I don't understand the reason either, because normally you hear something in advance.

‌



"It's also not the first time that something like this happens in the away section. It would be a shame for the benevolent supporters if we are punished with an empty away section.

"Our own goalkeeper gets a rocket at him and can just avoid him."

Sports.title: Man City 'pushing to sign Enzo Fernandez within days' as Chelsea's latest demands emerge
Sports.content:
Man City 'pushing to sign Enzo Fernandez within days' as Chelsea's latest demands emerge

Enzo Fernandez's future at Chelsea has been the subject of speculation throughout the campaign with Man City interested in the midfielder

View 2 Images Man City are reportedly pushing to sign Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea. (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

Manchester City are reportedly looking to complete the signing of Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez this week. According to Italian outlet Gianluca Di Marzio, Enzo Maresca's side are working on completing the formalities to bring the Argentinian to the Etihad Stadium.

‌



The report claims that Chelsea are asking for €140million (£120m) for the former Benfica man, with Fernandez pushing to reunite with the former Stamford Bridge chief. City are said to be in talks with Newcastle United over a move for Nico Gonzalez which would see the midfielder make the switch to the North East.

‌



Earlier this month, Chelsea set a deadline for Fernandez's departure, informing their Premier League rivals - and any possible suitors - that they had until 5pm on Friday, August 14 to seal a deal with the 25-year-old. No deal was struck and at the time, Maresca refused to be drawn on the speculation.

‌



He said: "In this moment I have to give you the same answer since day one, which will be always the same. He is a player from another club and I don't think it's correct to talk about other players.

"I'm not going to say anything about players who are not with us. Not today, to be honest. I don't think we're going to do something today."

‌



City came from behind to beat Bournemouth 2-1 in their Premier League opener while Chelsea make the short journey across West London to take on Fulham in their curtain-raiser. on Monday night. New head coach Xabi Alonso will be in the dugout for his first top-flight match in England when he comes up against former Liverpool teammate Alvaro Arbeloa.

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca worked with Fernandez during his time as Chelsea boss

All eyes will be on the starting 11 with the Spaniard tasked with taking Chelsea back towards the upper reaches of the Premier League after a topsy-turvy few years at Stamford Bridge. Whether Fernandez is in the starting line-up or not remains to be seen with speculation mounting over his future

‌



Chelsea were said to have agreed with his agent, Javier Pastore, that he could leave the Blues for £120million if the asking price was met by the August 14 deadline.

Alonso reaffirmed the stance that the 25-year-old remains a Chelsea player. He said:" Enzo is a Chelsea player. He's a top, top player.

"He's training really well. We are happy with him and he's getting ready for Monday."

Sports.title: Ex-Chelsea star Samuel Eto'o bizarrely pledges support to FIFA president Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
Ex-Chelsea star Samuel Eto'o bizarrely pledges support to FIFA president Gianni Infantino

FIFA President Gianni Infantino remains under huge pressure following his cancelled plan to sell a share of the World Cup to external investors but former Chelsea and Barcelona star Samuel Eto’o remains a fan

View 2 Images Samuel Eto'o has underlined his support for Gianni Infantino (Image: Getty Images)

Ex-Chelsea and Everton star Samuel Eto’o has bafflingly claimed that Gianni Infantino has ‘not done anything wrong’ in the wake of the growing scrutiny on the FIFA President.

‌



Infantino, 56, remains under huge pressure following his now failed plan to sell off a share of the World Cup to external investors. He performed a rapid u-turn on the plan, albeit UEFA have already confirmed a loss of confidence in his ability to lead FIFA. Even UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has criticised Infantino, claiming he is the wrong man to make decisions on the future of the game.

‌



A number of legendary players have now gone a step further by releasing a bombshell statement claiming that football has lost its core values under Infantino’s leadership.

‌



But one former star does not appear to be sharing that sentiment, having made clear his support of the current president.

Speaking to CNN Sports, former Chelsea and Barcelona striker Samuel Eto’o, said: “I don’t think that President Gianni Infantino has done anything wrong. I think the timing of all of that is because there’s an election coming out, when Gianni Infantino is standing. All of this has happened because there’s an election coming out, that’s all there is.”

‌



“President Gianni Infantino has changed football,” Eto’o added. “He’s given opportunities to nations that didn’t have those opportunities to take part in the most beautiful tournament, the World Cup. He enabled smaller nations to get seats at these competitions.

“He has helped our continent. He’s helped our federations to develop much more quickly, and we need to acknowledge that. We need to accept and recognize what he’s done, and we should support him for everything he’s done up to now.”

While Infantino’s plan garnered wide-spread criticism, Eto’o, who is president of the Cameroonian football federation, has actually claimed that it would have benefited his nation.

‌



View 2 Images Gianni Infantino remains under serious pressure (Image: Getty Images)

“The bigger nations took up the media space. They gave their point of view, and President Gianni Infantino wanted to keep the family of football together, and he decided to withdraw the project,” he said.

“I remain convinced that for us as Africans, this project was something that could have been incredible. It would have reset the balance of power in football to ensure that our talent doesn’t disappear and end up playing for other nations.

‌



“At the end of the day, those who have talked about the project and who’ve given their opinion haven’t properly read what it’s all about, and in some cases, they looked at it from their dominant position.

He added: “I want to see all of my colleagues, all of the presidents, re-reading the project. After President Infantino is re-elected, we will have the strength to ask for this project to be put back on the table for discussion.

“I remain convinced that, if there is a democratic vote, this project will be adopted because it’s good for the majority.”

Sports.title: Alexander Isak 'pretended he wasn't bothered' but Newcastle fans 'clearly upset him'
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak 'pretended he wasn't bothered' but Newcastle fans 'clearly upset him'

Liverpool striker Alexander Isak endured a tough time upon his return to St James' Park on Sunday

View 2 Images Alexander Isak was targeted by Newcastle fans on Sunday (Image: 2026 Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA)

It wasn't the return to St James' Park that Alexander Isak would have envisaged as Liverpool were held to a 2-2 draw at Newcastle United on Sunday. The Swedish star left the Magpies for the Reds last summer in a £125million deal, which stands as the British transfer record.

‌



Isak's expensive departure was acrimonious to say the least after he downed tools in order to engineer his move to Anfield. So, the stage was perhaps set for the forward to dish out retribution after he was verbally abused by sections of the Newcastle faithful upon arrival at his former stomping ground on Sunday afternoon.

‌



The Swedish international was jeered heavily when he left the Liverpool team coach to enter the stadium, with chants of 'rat' audible. Loud whistles and boos also accompanied his every touch during the game as he struggled to impose himself on proceedings.

‌



A body language expert has claimed Isak, upon arrival at Newcastle, was eager to "get away" from the fans who used to adore him. He's also been accused of trying to act as if he was unbothered by the hostility, when he "clearly was."

Darren Stanton said via OLBG: "Alexander Isak does something called lip suppression when he first arrives at St. James' Park. His lips are closed, pierced and slightly compressed. There's no arrival smile or anything like that from someone who is returning to his former home ground. He's very aware of the reception he's receiving and what is being chanted.

Virgil van Dijk sends Liverpool chiefs transfer message with Andoni Iraola in agreement READ MORE :

"The next thing I notice is that his eyebrows are slightly lowered, and he's looking downwards before entering the ground. This actually shows he wants to get away from the Newcastle fans as quickly as possible.

‌



"He's trying to act like he's not bothered by it, but he clearly is. When people don't look around, they try to imply that they are not bothered and that they don't care. It wouldn't surprise me if he wasn't actually listening to any music at all!

"With Isak, he comes across as very guarded and doesn't want any of us to read his emotions. He's like a stone and doesn't want to project anything. No anger, no excitement and no disgust. In terms of the way he is walking, it's quite purposeful. But he just wants to get away from it as quickly as possible.

Sports.title: Ollie Watkins transfer saga has turned ugly - but loyalty is a two-way street
Sports.content:
Ollie Watkins transfer saga has turned ugly - but loyalty is a two-way street

Ollie Watkins' time at Aston Villa could be up with the player supposedly choosing not to play on Sunday - but clubs and players can be equally disloyal when it suits them

View 3 Images Ollie Watkins looks to be trying to force Aston Villa's hand (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

The transfer window can be a particularly bruising time for players, egos and reputations. And there is unlikely to be too much sympathy from Aston Villa fans for Ollie Watkins after Unai Emery ’s post-match comments.

‌



Villa lose 4-0 at Brighton, the club has been left in a bit of a mess (again) by a messy transfer window which has seen big-name departures like Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa, Lucas Digne and Morgan Rogers with Emiliano Martinez likely to follow.

‌



So, the Watkins story - a live transfer target for Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal - certainly meant people are talking about the Villa striker rather than a humiliating defeat. A distraction tactic?

‌



It has made Watkins the villain of the piece with Emery hinting heavily - but not quite saying it out right - that the England striker refused to play at Brighton.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Watkins, 30, is being offered a huge contract in the Saudi Pro League, it would be a fantastic pay day for a player who has reached the very top in his career having really battled his way up from non-league. This is a really nice, understated but determined player who does not really seek the spotlight but there have been ups and downs at Villa.

‌



It has largely always been up when he is on the pitch because he works hard, scores goals and gives his all for the team. He has enjoyed success with the Europa League and helping the club qualify for the Champions League.

The downs have been when he has been dropped, he has been left out on numerous occasions and when players are axed from the team no-one stands up for them.

It’s just when the suggestion comes they don’t want to play for the team. Emery is such a good manager and one of the reasons is because he’s a bad loser. He’s so determined to win. As the saying goes, show me a good loser and I’ll show you a loser. Emery is a winner.

‌



View 3 Images Unai Emery didn't shy away from addressing Ollie Watkins' situation (Image: Joris Verwijst/Soccrates/Getty Images)

After the Brighton game, you could see he was fuming, Watkins was caught in the crossfire and is now public enemy No.1. It was Villa who denied Watkins a move to Arsenal in January 2025 when the Midlands club did need to sell. Arsenal will always say that it was Villa who first sounded them out. Villa eventually sold Jhon Duran to balance the books.

Watkins was priced out of a move but, like all players, is a commodity who is owned by his club - until they don’t want him. Then he’s just discarded. Villa have sold so many players this summer that it must have created some uncertainty. If you look at what happened last season - they did not win any of their first five Premier League games and scored just one goal - this transfer carousel is not new.

‌



They have been prolific buyers and sellers. And so is Watkins so wrong? There is no way a player should go on strike to force a move when they are paid so well in the first place.

View 3 Images Morgan Rogers is one of several high profile sales made by Aston Villa (Image: Darren Walsh, Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

But is it always that black and white? You can be sure players up and down the country will be talking with their clubs, agents and managers about what the future holds.

‌



Many players will feel as if they need to move on. This is not the era of player power. But we have seen a shift of more clubs openly courting transfer targets - even if they are under contract.

Every club does it and if that turns the odd head - especially when a move would be for life-changing money - then they probably are not in the right frame of mind to play.

But equally, the player will probably recall the last time they were dropped and ask their own questions about loyalty. It must be a two-way street. Clearly, Villa fans might not agree right now. But this saga has probably happened at every club this summer - but not so publicly.

Sports.title: Rod Stewart rocks up to support his local non-league football team
Sports.content:
Rod Stewart rocks up to support his local non-league football team

Rod Stewart is such a massive football fan he paid £10 to support his local non-league side Bishop's Stortford and watch son's friend

Rod Stewart turns up at non-league football match

Rock legend Sir Rod Stewart is such a passionate football fan he was spotted in a crowd of 322 watching his local non-league side. The singer paid his £10 entrance, the reduced admission fee for over 60s, and watched the match between Bishop’s Stortford and Alvechurch.

‌



Rod was in the crowd to support Stortford’s right back Joe Nardelli - one of son Alastair’s best friends. Bishop's Stortford chairman Ian Kettridge said: “It was great for Rod to come and watch us.

‌



"We were just sorry we couldn’t give him a home win! He was really friendly and took time to speak to fans from both teams and joined in the banter."

‌



Sir Rod Stewart all smiles at Celtic game after being forced to cancel gigs over heart surgery READ MORE :

Penny Lancaster issues tribute to Rod Stewart as he undergoes heart surgery READ MORE :

View 4 Images Rod Stewart poses for selfie with Alvechurch fan (Image: Peter Bromley)

Mr Kettridge added: “He’s very welcome any time here at the Grundon Community stadium.” Rod chatted with fellow fans, posed for selfies and shook the hand of Stortford’s popular owner Steve Smith. Alvechurch won the Pitching In Southern League Premier Central contest 3-0.

When Alvechurch scored their second goal their small army of fans, who were standing in front of Rod, cheekily started singing his classic hit: “We are Sailing.”

‌



View 4 Images Bishop's Stortford's chairman Ian Kettridge said the star was welcome at the ground 'any time'

Before the match the crowd and both sides joined in a minute’s applause for Stortford supporter Dave Ewart who had passed away suddenly earlier in the week. Rod, a passionate Scotland and Celtic fan, left shortly before the end to head to his home nearby.

Alvechurch fan Terry Bennett, 47, from Birmingham said: “I shook his hand and congratulated him on beating cancer. He was very friendly. I told him I had oesophagus cancer and he asked me about that. What a great surprise to see a music legend at a non league game. It really made our day.”

‌



View 4 Images Rod Stewart shaking hand of fan at Bishop's Stortford FC

Bishop’s Stortford FC ia one of the oldest football clubs in the country - being formed back in 1874. They celebrated their 150th anniversary in 2024 with many former players returning including Dwight Gayle who went on to play for Newcastle United and Crystal Palace among other clubs. They are the last holders of the FA Amateur Cup winning at Wembley in 1974. And they won the FA Trophy at Wembley in 1981 with former Arsenal legend John Radford in the side.

View 4 Images "Allez les Bleus" - Stortford's loyal army of fans when the Daily Mirror sponsored their FA Cup game (Image: Daily Mirror)

Article continues below

The club is unique because a county boundary runs through the pitch meaning a player can score a goal in Essex in the first half and Hertfordshire in the second. Back in 2013 the Daily Mirror sponsored Stortford in the FA Cup first round when they played Northampton Town which was selected for a live TV game.

Sports.title: Wirtz and a worst-ever transfer window? Carra's damning Liverpool verdict
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher says he doesn't see where Florian Wirtz fits into the Liverpool team - and the £116.5m German could be part of the worst transfer window in Premier League history.

During a damning assessment of the Reds' midfield set-up in their 2-2 draw at Newcastle, Carragher also explained the big weakness in new boss Andoni Iraola's tactical approach at Liverpool and why it will prevent them from launching a Premier League title challenge this season.

Here's how the Sky Sports pundit broke down Liverpool's big issues on Monday Night Football...

A midfield dilemma

"I don't believe that midfield can function with the personnel in there," said Carragher. "For me, it doesn't work. And it's not just about personnel, it's the structure the manager is asking."

Image: Jamie Carragher highlights the Liverpool midfield against Newcastle

Liverpool fielded Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai in midfield at St James' Park, with Florian Wirtz at No 10.

However, rather than sitting in a double pivot, Szoboszlai often moved forward into more attacking areas.

Carragher noted how Man City have had success in the past with a double-pivot and No 10 set-up but added: "Why did [Pep] Guardiola always bring his full-backs inside? Because the holding midfield player needed help to stop counter-attacks. Straight away that's a problem for me [with Liverpool].

Image: Jamie Carragher was critical of Ryan Gravenberch's decision to burst forward from a holding role, leaving Liverpool's midfield open

Image: Jamie Carragher points out how Dominik Szoboszlai moved ahead of the ball - leaving Liverpool vulnerable to a counter-attack

Carragher showed examples of not only Szoboszlai but also Gravenberch charging forwards to join Wirtz and emptying the midfield - providing space for Newcastle to counter-attack into.

"All they think about is going forwards. All three of them. And that's why it can't work," said Carragher.

"I don't think I've ever seen a more offensive team, or players who think offensively in the Premier League than that. There's only the two centre-backs who don't think about going forward."

Image: Jamie Carragher illustrates how 35-year-old Virgil van Dijk opted not to push up, leaving space for Newcastle to exploit

Carragher also noted how it appears to be an instruction from Iraola for Wirtz and Szoboszlai to 'lock on' to opposition midfielders.

However, while Brentford had success employing a similarly aggressive tactic against Tottenham because their centre-backs stepped up to close the space behind, Liverpool's Virgil van Dijk didn't make the same move. Instead, the 35-year-old centre-back sat deeper.

"You've got a situation, like at Man Utd under Erik ten Hag a few years ago - a team who want to press high but with a deep block.

"That's why these big holes are appearing. The midfield players want to lock on and Van Dijk does not want to come with them."

On Van Dijk, Carragher added: "He needs protecting, he needs cuddling, he needs looking after."

Holding midfield signing essential

After watching Liverpool against Newcastle, Carragher says it is now essential they sign a holding midfielder to offer them more security against fast breaks.

"Liverpool need someone alongside Gravenberch," said Carragher. "It doesn't necessarily need to be a player who can't get on the ball and he's just tackling and stopping players. If you play for one of the top teams in the world, you need to be able to get hold of the ball. But I want someone who can run.

"Szboszlai has to go to the No 10."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Newcastle and Liverpool.

What to do with Wirtz?

If a holding midfielder comes in alongside Gravenberch and Szoboszlai goes to No 10, where does Wirtz go?

Carragher doesn't see a suitable role for him in the Liverpool team with Iraola's set-up.

He says the German's lack of end product with Liverpool - just five goals and three assists in 33 Premier League appearances last season - means it is fair to question whether he will ever be the answer.

"This thing that it takes people a year to settle in the Premier League, I think is a bit of a myth. I don't think there's too many examples where it does," said Carragher.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville says Liverpool's Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz have been given enough time and must now start delivering. Neville says the pair are 'too nice' and wants to see Wirtz have a much greater influence in the final third.

"I've always seen this coming. When people are saying [Wirtz] has got to go to No 10, that means Szoboszlai's got to be in the team and he's not a central midfield player.

"I thought this would come up in six weeks, I think it's coming up right now. I don't see where he fits in at all, really.

"What's Iraola going to do with Wirtz? You can't keep going with it, it's not working,

"It didn't work last season. Liverpool last season conceded 78 goals, 53 in the Premier League, the most they've ever conceded in the Premier League. And all of a sudden it's all about buying wingers?

"I'm not sure where he fits. I almost thought you could put him in a pocket from the left, where he plays for Germany, but Iraola loves wingers, he wants players who've got energy up and down the flank.

"I don't think we're seeing a massive underperformance. I think what we've seen for a year is probably what he is, which is a neat and tidy footballer. Not a player who should be worth £110m, someone who probably should be £50m-60m, something like that. Neat and tidy, lovely touch. I'm not sure what people are expecting."

Worst transfer window in Premier League history?

Image: Liverpool's transfer signings in the summer of 2025

Wirtz was part of an enormous £445m transfer spend by Liverpool last summer, when it appeared they were out to supercharge Arne Slot's Premier League title-winning squad. Instead it went badly wrong, with Liverpool limping home in fifth, with Slot sacked.

As well as Wirtz, Liverpool also signed Alexander Isak for a Premier League record £125m, Hugo Ekitike (£79m), Milos Kerkez (£40m), Jeremie Frimpong (£29.5m), Giorgi Mamardashvili (£29m) and Giovanni Leoni (£26m).

Carragher reckons that transfer window may have hurt Liverpool more than it helped them. In fact, he reckons it could go down as the worst summer of business by a Premier League club ever.

"My fear is this window of 12 months ago could set Liverpool back a year or two to fix it," he said.

"Don't forget, last season it was not about these players. Because it was all about Arne Slot and his style of playing, and he's not like Jurgen Klopp, and he's holding his players back...

"But we're talking 12 months of under-performance from all of these players except Ekitike.

"If this doesn't change in the next two or three months, under Iraola, and these players improve, I think we're going to be looking at that as arguably the worst transfer window we've probably seen in Premier League history.

"When you consider the fees for these players, and what it was going to do for Liverpool... The idea wasn't for these players coming in just to be good players, it was to create something like a little dynasty for Liverpool.

"Let's not forget, Liverpool won the league two years ago. These were supposed to do what City have done in the last few years, or Manchester United in the past, where they've gone and won two or three leagues in five years."

Title contenders? Not this year...

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Carragher believes Liverpool boast a stronger starting eleven than Manchester United heading into the 2026/27 Premier League season, but says the Reds still need to add depth and quality before the transfer window closes.

With all that in mind, Carragher has little hope of his former club mounting a serious title challenge this season.

"I don't think Liverpool will be contenders this season," he said. "Liverpool are in transition

"I'm not trying to make excuses for them, because they've lost [Mohamed] Salah, Van Dijk is probably going to go, maybe this is his last season, and the goalkeeper Alisson. You're talking about three all-time greats there for Liverpool.

"So they're probably not going to be there in 12 months and these [signings of summer 2025] have got to find their feet, and Iraola has got to find his feet at a big club.

"For me, if Liverpool qualify for the Champions League this season, I'd be happy. The manager sort of beds in and then you can maybe go from there and look to challenge."

Sports.title: Man City interested in Gakpo
Sports.content:
Manchester City are interested in signing Tottenham target Cody Gakpo from Liverpool.

City are looking at options to improve their forward line, with Savinho - and potentially Omar Marmoush - set to join Tottenham.

There have not been any club-to-club talks between City and Liverpool at this stage for Gakpo, who is under contract at Anfield until 2030.

Liverpool do not want to sell Gakpo as things stand and would likely need to bring in two wide forwards to be comfortable with letting him go.

The 27-year-old started and scored in the Reds' Premier League opener against Newcastle last weekend.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Newcastle and Liverpool.

They have been pursuing deals for PSG duo Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye, while they have had multiple offers rejected for Brighton's Yankuba Minteh.

Man City have already verbally agreed a deal with Palmeiras to sign Allan for £34m as a replacement for Savinho. Spurs have agreed to pay up to £85m for Savinho, who had a medical last week.

Sky Sports News reported last week that a deal for Marmoush was very close to being agreed by City and Spurs. He was named on the bench for City's Premier League opener against Bournemouth but did not come on.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan and Michael Bridge discuss whether Manchester City need to sign another midfielder alongside Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi?

Man City reach Allan agreement

Latest from Sky Sports News' Ben Ransom and Zinny Boswell:

Manchester City have reached an agreement with Palmeiras over the signing of Allan.

The deal for the winger is worth up to £34m. City are paying fixed fee of £32m plus £2m in add-ons.

Both clubs have a verbal agreement, but are yet to exchange documents for the 22-year-old's transfer.

The player will be given permission to travel for a medical once this process has been completed to the satisfaction of both clubs.

Allan is being brought in to replace his fellow Brazilian Savinho, who is set to join Tottenham in a deal worth up to £85m.

now 17.07 EDT Jacob Steinberg This was a crash course for Xabi Alonso in life at Chelsea. His new side thrilled in possession at Craven Cottage. The front three of João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers combined to devastating effect and there was even an assist for the new £52m centre-back, Maxence Lacroix. At times the only issue was the two No 10s both laying claim to the ice cold celebration. Palmer had a point to prove after missing out on England’s World Cup squad and Rogers scored on his debut after his £117m move from Aston Villa. Yet victory in Alonso’s first competitive game as Chelsea’s manager was far from straightforward. He saw that he needs a better goalkeeper than Robert Sánchez and will worry about his side’s lack of smarts. Fulham, who will hope this bright start under Alvaro Arbeloa shows there is life after Marco Silva, were unfortunate not to rescue a point. Sports.title: ‘Enough is enough’: players pile pressure on under-fire Gianni Infantino to resign
Sports.content:
A group of influential current and former footballers have added to the pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa, saying “enough is enough” in a statement shared widely across social media.

The intervention is particularly significant given some of those behind its circulation have undertaken ambassadorial activities for Fifa as part of its “Fifa Legends” programme. Among them is the former Manchester United and Arsenal defender Mikaël Silvestre, who also sits on the governing body’s 16-member players’ voice panel designed to assist with anti-racism initiatives.

Others to have shared the statement include the England defender Lucy Bronze, the former England keeper David James and the France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit. More signatories are expected to follow in a concerted reaction to Infantino’s ill-fated attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup.

“We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” part of the statement read. “Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under Fifa’s current leadership. For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

“Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football. Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.”

The group called for efforts to “reshape the future of our sport”, adding: “There are good people within Fifa who want to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structured change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run. Those who step on to the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine voice to help reshape football’s future together.”

Infantino has resisted calls to resign and spent Saturday at a youth tournament in the Dominican Republic, attempting to smooth relations with some of the smaller Caribbean member associations on whose support his fate may hinge.

One former player with a different perspective on Infantino is the former Real Madrid, Barcelona and Chelsea striker Samuel Eto’o, who is president of the Cameroonian football federation. In an interview with CNN, Eto’o said Infantino had not committed any missteps and called for the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme to be put back on the table if Infantino is re-elected next March. He said the money from FFE would “reset the balance of power” in football and ensure African countries avoided losing top players to other national teams.
