World.title: Violence flares in Haiti as gang attack kills 30 people
World.content:
Island nation grapples with violence as it seeks to hold first elections in more than a decade.

At least 30 people have been killed as a new wave of violence grips Haiti.

A powerful gang coalition mounted the deadly attack on a farming community in Kenscoff, south of the capital, Port-au-Prince, late on Sunday, officials reported. The flare-up in violence comes as Haiti hopes to hold its first general election in more than a decade.

Jean Massillon, Kenscoff’s mayor, said armed men “sowed chaos” as they set homes on fire and killed residents.

He said gang members targeted a church and homes, including that of Jean William Pape, a leading public health expert.

Massillon blamed the attack on members of Viv Ansanm, a group that was designated as a “foreign terrorist organisation” by the United States government last year.

Gangs control an estimated 70 percent of Port-au-Prince. Viv Ansanm has repeatedly targeted Kenscoff, which occupies a strategic position overlooking routes into Petion-Ville, where several embassies, upscale hotels and ⁠the temporary seat of government are located.

A United Nations-backed gang suppression force is mandated to help police fight the gangs and restore order, but it has not yet reached its full capacity of 5,500 members.

According to the UN, gang violence has displaced 1.5 million people across Haiti. The violence has persisted despite efforts to rein it in. More than 3,100 people were reported killed and 1,189 injured from January to June as gangs continued a reign of terror in Port-au-Prince that sparked international concern last year.

Haiti’s prime minister’s office on Monday condemned the “heinous attack” and sought to reassure Haitians that security forces were on high alert and reinforcements were being deployed.



“Kenscoff will not be abandoned,” a statement read. “The government’s authority will be restored, ⁠without weakness and without delay.”

Haitians have been registering to vote in elections planned in January, but experts have warned it’s currently too dangerous to hold the vote.

World.title: Ex-Liverpool star Fabinho reunited with Mohamed Salah at Trabzonspor
World.content:
Fabinho joined ​Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ittihad in 2023, where he won the country’s domestic football ​league after his five-year stint at Liverpool.

Brazil ⁠midfielder Fabinho has ⁠signed a two-year deal with Trabzonspor, the Turkish Super Lig football side has announced, and will link up with ⁠former Liverpool teammate Mohamed Salah.

The 32-year-old midfielder will receive a 2.6-million-euro ($3.03m) guaranteed fee and a 1.4-million-euro ($1.63m) signing ⁠fee per season, according to a Turkish stock exchange filing made by the team on Monday.

“An agreement has been reached for a two-year contract with … Fabinho, who is currently in free status,” Trabzonspor posted on ‌X.

Fabinho joined Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ittihad in 2023 and helped the team win the domestic league after his five-year stint at Liverpool.

“A really special feeling to be playing with Salah again … I had the opportunity to play with him for five years in Liverpool. He is a person whom I respect a lot both for ⁠what he has done and what he ⁠will do,” Fabinho said after arriving at Trabzon airport earlier on Monday.

Looking to reignite his chemistry with 34-year-old Salah, Fabinho said: “I will always try to do the ⁠best I can with whatever ability I have.

“Along with the experience and leadership that come from ⁠playing for so many years, I will ⁠always try to help my teammates.”

Fabinho made 219 appearances for Liverpool, helping it win the Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup, League Cup, Club World Cup and UEFA Super Cup ‌titles.

Egypt forward Salah joined Trabzonspor as a free agent earlier this month.

Trabzonspor finished third in the Turkish top flight last season, and take on Hungary’s Ferencvaros on Thursday in the second leg of their Europa League playoff tie, trailing 1-0.

World.title: Washington Post ordered to rehire Karen Attiah after Charlie Kirk posts
World.content:
Karen Attiah was fired for posts about Charlie Kirk’s assassination that the Post said violated its social media policy.

An independent arbitrator has ordered the Washington Post to reinstate opinion columnist Karen Attiah and award her back pay after finding the newspaper lacked sufficient grounds to fire her.

Attiah was dismissed in September 2025 following social media posts about the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk. Attiah’s firing came amid a broader conservative campaign seeking professional consequences for people whose comments about Kirk’s assassination were deemed offensive.

“This decision confirms what we’ve said from the start: I was doing my job as an opinion writer, and this was wrongful termination,” Attiah said in a statement. “After spending over a decade of my career at the Post as an editor and an opinion columnist focusing on race, gender and global human rights, I’m relieved to finally have that record set straight.”

The decision was issued by private arbitrator Sarah Miller Espinosa, according to a copy obtained by Attiah’s lawyers and cited by US media. Espinosa determined that the Post had violated its labor agreement and did not have adequate cause to terminate Attiah.

“The Washington Post failed to establish the grievant engaged in gross misconduct,” Espinosa wrote.

The dispute stemmed from posts Attiah made on Bluesky after Kirk was killed in September 2025. In one post, she referenced past comments Kirk had made about Black women.

The Post subsequently said in Attiah’s termination letter that her posts breached its social media policy. The policy requires employees to ensure their online conduct remains respectful and does not damage the integrity of the newspaper’s journalism.

The ruling comes amid wider questions about the direction of the Post under Bezos, who in February 2025 announced the opinion section would reshape its editorial focus around themes of personal liberties and free markets.



The Post has also faced financial pressures. In February, the newspaper announced layoffs affecting about a third of its workforce, with cuts reaching its international, editing, metro and sports desks as the company dealt with mounting financial losses.

World.title: Iran faces 'greatest financial offensive ever', says US treasury secretary
World.content:
The US announced a host of sanctions against Iran and threatened its supporters in what Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said was "the single greatest financial offensive ever".

Labelling it an "economic D-Day" for Iran, Bessent said the US would sever all economic ties with the country and added that any nation financially partnering with Iran would also be isolated.

However, the latest threat to the Iranian regime follows several U-turns and extended deadlines from the White House in its efforts to end the conflict.

The war has led to hikes in global oil prices, and in response to the latest threat Iran warned it would shut down all oil exports from the region if the war continued.

The Iranian regime has also issued a fresh warning to shipping to not pass through the Strait of Hormuz without its permission, according to Reuters.

One fifth of the world's oil and gas usually passes through strait, a narrow waterway south of Iran, but the flow has been effectively blocked by the country since the conflict began at the end of February, leading to higher oil prices globally.

At a press conference on Monday outlining what has been called "Operation Economic Outcast", Bessent said the US was launching an "economic onslaught against Iran's financial connections around the globe".

"Iran now faces a very clear choice with only two paths before them: complete global isolation....or a path back to normalcy with an opportunity to rejoin the global economy," he said.

The treasury secretary claimed America was "no longer managing the Iranian threat, we are ending it".

Bessent said the Treasury Department had mapped networks, facilitators and financial channels used by Iran to evade sanctions to trade oil.

The department said it has issued determinations against five sectors: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping. The Treasury has also imposed sanctions on almost 60 entities, individuals and vessels.

Bessent said that such actions would "tighten the noose and block every potential source of revenue" for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the wider Iranian regime.

In a warning to governments and entities assisting or trading with Iran, he said they could not "claim they are blind to enabling this activity".

He declined to highlight specific countries, but said Trump would be phoning world leaders "with specific request to cease their interactions with the regime."

While he said it was important to give people time to understand the new sanctions, he added: "they should know that that will move very quickly and that we are serious."

World.title: UK PM Burnham vows support for Ukraine despite 'outrageous threats' from Russia
World.content:
Burnham said allies were doing "everything we can" to "dig into our own stocks and help others dig into their stocks" of air defences to protect Ukraine.

"This is the moment to keep up the pressure on Russia, the moment to squeeze their ability to fund this illegal war," Burnham said, praising the "strength" of the Ukrainian people.

"Ukraine has been Europe's protector, not a drain on our security but the front line in keeping Europe safe."

It comes after Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov criticised the UK's decision to share the missile blueprints. Peskov said it prevented "even the slightest progress" towards achieving peace.

He told reporters on Monday that the Russian military was already gathering data to locate any missile production sites to destroy them.

"Britain is involved in this war on the side of the Kyiv regime. Britain methodically and regularly adds fuel to the fire," he added.

In response, Burnham said: "Who started the fire? That's the question, isn't it?"

He said the issue of missile interceptors would be the main topic at the coalition of the willing meeting.

World.title: Russia's second-biggest online retailer targeted in Ukrainian strikes
World.content:
Meanwhile, Ozon workers in Adygeysk, in the Adygea region, and Nevinnomyssk, in the Stavropol region, have been evacuated.

Videos posted on social media of the Ozon attacks have been verified by the BBC. One shows a drone hitting a warehouse in the Orenburg region, while another shows a large plume of smoke and flames rising from its warehouse in Dagestan.

Shares in Ozon fell by as much as 12% on the Moscow Exchange on Monday morning, while shares in its major shareholder, private equity firm AFK Sistema, fell by almost 13%.

When asked on Monday whether the Russian government would provide state support to Ozon, the Kremlin said it was "working with business representatives to develop various options for providing support in this difficult situation".

The overnight strikes comes a day after Ozon's site in the Samara region was hit. The company said a number of its workers had been injured.

Following that strike, Ukraine's defence ministry said on Saturday: "Systematic strikes on dual-use goods storage centres complicate the enemy's logistics and negatively affect the Russian economy as a whole.

"After Ukrainian units hit 15 of the largest logistics hubs of Wildberries, it was Ozon's turn."

Meanwhile, in Ukraine's Odesa region, overnight strikes targeted food storage facilities and energy infrastructure leading to five people being injured, the region's head Oleg Kiper said on Telegram.

Founded in 1998, Ozon is one of Russia's first online retailers. The company is second only to Wildberries in terms of scale and presence, with its pick-up posts and delivery boxes stationed across the country.

Both the Ozon and Wildberries logos are often seen together in Russia at shared pick-up points.

The targeting of these online retailers has had the effect of bringing the war closer to ordinary Russians.

Both companies have been described as "Russia's Amazon" and it is estimated that they are used by 85-90% of Russia's economically active population.

In many remote places lacking accessible shops, Russians depend on them for much of their clothes and household appliances.

But unlike Amazon, which sells goods directly alongside its marketplace business, Wildberries and Ozon act almost entirely as marketplaces, connecting independent sellers with buyers across Russia, storing and delivering their goods and handling payments.

This means many of the losses incurred in the attacks have been borne by those businesses.

The Kremlin has denied that online platforms are used for army supplies.

World.title: Israel warns of 'forceful' response to kites flown from Gaza
World.content:
Four kites were found in Kibbutz Nahal Oz, which is about 800m (2,620ft) from the Gaza border, on Friday and Saturday. Several more were found elsewhere in southern Israel last week, according to local media.

The Israeli reports cited military sources as saying they believed Hamas was behind the kites and that they might have been intended to test Israel's response.

No suspicious materials were attached to the kites and they did not pose a threat, the military said.

But Katz warned there would be "zero tolerance" and said: "A balloon is treated like a kite, and a kite is treated like a drone, with or without explosives."

Residents of Nahal Oz said in a statement that they feared the return of incendiary kites and balloons, adding: "We will not accept a policy of containment when it comes to our security."

Hamas warned of "the danger of the allegations and threats" from Israel and said the kites were "basically children's toys from displacement camps".

"These threats are based on fabricated pretexts and are an attempt to justify the continuation of the aggression and violations against our people," a spokesman for the group added.

On Sunday, Palestinian health officials said two people were killed and seven others injured in two Israeli strikes in Nuseirat refugee camp and the town of al-Zawayda, both in central Gaza.

A four-year-old boy called Mohammed Taha was killed when a building in al-Zawayda, just north of Maghazi refugee camp, was bombed, according to local media.

The Israeli military said it killed the commander of a Hamas weapons manufacturing site in the Maghazi area, whom it identified as Ismail Abu Ful, and that it had warned the residents to evacuate beforehand.

"There is no ceasefire, there is nothing," Abu Ahmed, a displaced man who had been sheltering nearby, told Reuters news agency. "We want solutions, we want to live in peace."

On Monday, Palestinian media reported that a man called Mohammed Abu Asad was killed in an overnight Israeli strike on a tent in the central town of Deir al-Balah.

The Israeli military said Abu Asad was a member of the elite Nukhba forces of Hamas's military wing who had taken part in the Hamas-led 7 October 2023 attack on southern Israel.

The Israeli military launched a campaign in Gaza in response to the cross-border assault, during which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 were taken hostage.

More than 74,420 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since then, including 1,288 since the ceasefire took effect, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry.

World.title: King of Norway's health has worsened, palace says
World.content:
King Harald V of Norway's health has worsened, the palace has said, as he remains in hospital receiving antibiotics for a bacterial infection in his bloodstream.

The monarch has responded to treatment despite the deterioration in his condition, according to the palace, but he will remain at Oslo University Hospital, Rikshospitalet, and on leave from royal duties until further notice.

The 89-year-old, who has been on the throne since 1991, was admitted to hospital and put on sick leave a week ago.

His son, Crown Prince Haakon, 53, has been serving as regent while his father is on leave.

King Harald has been treated in recent weeks with cortisone for a rare blood condition, haemolytic anaemia. It causes the number of red blood cells in the body to be reduced, and leads to fatigue and shortness of breath.

In April 2024, Norway's royal household said that King Harald would make a "permanent reduction" to his public engagements "out of consideration for his age". That year, the king had been fitted with a pacemaker after falling ill on holiday in Malaysia.

The Norwegian royal family has already faced a challenging year in 2026.

Crown Prince Haakon's wife, Crown Princess Mette-Marit, received a lung transplant in June after she had been diagnosed with a rare form of pulmonary fibrosis in 2018.

The transplant came two days after Mette-Marit's son Marius Borg HÃ¸iby was sentenced to four years in prison after being convicted of two counts of rape. He had denied the most serious charges and his lawyers said he would appeal the sentence.

HÃ¸iby, 29, was four when his mother married Crown Prince Haakon and is not himself a royal figure.

Also earlier in the year, documents were released revealing Mette-Marit's frequent contact with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

She later apologised to Norway's king and queen for her three-year friendship with Epstein and admitted to "poor judgement", adding in a national TV interview that she wished she had never met him.

World.title: Outrage in Nepal over rape and murder of three-year-old girl
World.content:
Activists and politicians in Nepal have urged the government to enact tougher laws as the alleged rape and murder of a three-year-old girl has caused outrage across the country.

Nepal has seen continued protests since the girl was found dead last week, three days after she went missing in Madhesh province.

Nine people have been arrested in connection with the case, a local police spokesman told the BBC.

The crime has triggered demands for reform. Police have also been accused of negligence in the initial stages of the investigation after footage of a teenage suspect was leaked onto social media.

After days of demonstrations in the city of Simara, the victim's family met government ministers, and secured a written agreement over the weekend.

The government has promised to review laws on serious offences, and create a memorial in honour of the child.

The incident has also opened a wider debate over how Nepal deals with young offenders, with some campaigners pushing for harsher punishments for minors convicted of rape or murder.

Prominent human rights activist Gauri Pradhan called the attack a "very painful incident and the government should punish anyone involved in such atrocious act. There should be some serious efforts for wider reforms".

However, he cautioned against calls for the introduction of the death penalty.

There has also been anger after a video showing a teenage suspect giving a statement about the suspected murder was uploaded to social media, sparking questions as to how footage of the individual under police custody was leaked.

"We have so far found one police personnel directly involved in the [leak] and have initiated action against him," chief district officer of Bara district, Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, told the BBC.

"If more officers are found, they will also be punished. We have zero tolerance against such practice."

More than 25,500 accusations of rape and sexual abuse were filed between July 2017 to July 2025, according to Nepalese Police.

Of these cases, more than 3,200 female victims were under the age of 10, the police say.

World.title: Nearly three million Teslas recalled in China over hidden door handles
World.content:
Minimalistic door handles became a signature feature of electric vehicles (EVs), but the controversial designs are now at the centre of China's biggest car recall, affecting more than 4 million vehicles.

The recall, which includes 2.98 million Chinese-made Teslas, follows safety concerns that the hidden door handles are difficult to locate and open in emergency situations.

Other brands affected by the recall include Chinese carmakers XPeng, Xiaomi and Geely.

The recalled vehicles will have a warning label stuck on the interior door and receive a software update to automatically lower the windows in a crash.

The designs have come under scrutiny after two fatal crashes in China involving Xiaomi EVs, in which power failures were suspected to have prevented doors from being opened.

Tesla said in a statement on Friday that it was recalling some of its Model 3, Y, S and X vehicles due to door handles that are "difficult to identify and operate because their colour is similar to the interior trim".

"In extreme situations such as a severe collision causing the vehicle's low-voltage system to fail, this could hinder occupants from quickly opening the doors to escape and impede rescue efforts by those outside the vehicle, posing a safety hazard," it said.

Tesla said it would place warning labels on the recalled vehicles and issue a software update to automatically lower a vehicle's windows after a collision.

It is not clear if the affected firms plan to make a similar recall for the rest of the world.

The BBC has contacted Tesla, XPeng, Xiaomi and Geely for comment.

The use of hidden handle designs has "snowballed" after Chinese brands were quick to copy the "sleek" look of Tesla's Model S sedan since 2014, said Tu Le, the founder of consultancy Sino Auto Insights.

The use of warning labels and a software update is more of a "band-aid" than a lasting solution for the issue, he added.

In February, Chinese authorities announced a ban on hidden door handles.

Under new rules due to take effect on 1 January 2027, cars will only be allowed to be sold in China if they have a mechanical release on both the inside and outside of their doors.

Tesla's door handles were also involved in a probe by US safety regulators after reports that they suddenly stopped working, leaving children trapped in the cars.

In July, the US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration suggested creating a new formal safety standard for all carmakers.

The BBC has contacted the agency for comment.

World.title: Sonya Massey's killer Sean Grayson dies in US prison
World.content:
Sean Grayson, the white US police officer convicted of murdering a black woman, Sonya Massey, during an incident at her home in 2024, has died in prison at age 32.

Grayson shot dead Massey, 36, during an exchange that took place after she reported a suspected intruder at her residence in Illinois. The killing reignited the debate about police brutality in the US.

Grayson said he fired because he thought Massey was about to throw a pot of boiling water on him. He was last year found guilty of second-degree murder.

The former police officer was undergoing treatment for colon cancer. His lawyer Daniel Fultz confirmed to the BBC that Grayson had died on Sunday, but did not disclose the cause.

The BBC has asked the Illinois Department of Corrections for comment.

Lawyers for Massey's family said: "Grayson's death in custody from cancer does not bring Sonya back."

"We wish his family prayers of peace, as we do for all who grieve a loved one. Sonya's family knows that pain all too well and will grieve her loss the rest of their days," the lawyers said, according to CBS News, the BBC's US partner.

Protests took place across the US in the aftermath of Massey's death, and then-President Joe Biden declared that the late woman "should be alive today".

World.title: Excitement as Gov Oyebanji installs Ekiti community monarch after 25 years
World.content:
There was jubilation in Oke Ako in the Ikole Local Government Area of Ekiti State on Monday as Governor Biodun Oyebanji installed the new monarch of the community, the Owa of Oke-Ako, Oba Bamidele Olanrewaju.

Before last week’s approval and subsequent installation of Mr Oni as the new royal father of the community, the traditional stool was vacant for over 25 years.

Governor Oyebanji, represented by his deputy, Monisade Afuye, at the presentation of Staff of Office and Instrument of Appointment to the new monarch, who is from Oke Aofin Royal Dynasty, congratulated the monarch and the town for overcoming the difficulties witnessed during the interregnum.

The governor said, “I want to congratulate all of you today on this glorious moment. This, to us, is victory at last. You didn’t have a traditional ruler for over 25 years, but today, you are celebrating one after overcoming all past challenges.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I want you to look at the back, take stock and look for way to make up for the lost grounds. The best way for you to do this is by allowing peace, unity and love. No town can develop without these.”

The governor, who warned against unwarranted internal strife and acrimony in the town, appealed to other contestants to “partner with the new traditional ruler to rev up the pedal of unity and development and create a vista of recognition for Oke Ako among the comity of towns in Ekiti”.

The governor said the long drawn legal battles that accompanied the selection process caused a major impediment that prevented government from exercising the statutory and legal procedures that could speed up the enthronement of a new monarch since the demise of Oba Omotayo Ogunbiyi, from the Okediosan Ruling House, on December 10, 2000.

He praised the Regent, Tinuade Ogunbiyi-Adebayo, who presided over the community for over 25 years as well the people of the town for always identifying with progressive leadership, urging them to bring such spirit to bear in working with the new monarch to attract development to Oke Ako.

The Ekiti governor stated, “I want you to work with Kabiyesi to restore the glory of Oke Ako. With all of you working together as a team, this town will become prosperous, progressive and successful. Kindly do all within your powers to cooperate with him for the benefit of all of you.”

The new monarch, Mr Oni, in his acceptance speech, lauded the state government, kingmakers and royal families on the installation of a new monarch after the interregnum, promising to work hard and justify the confidence reposed in him.

Commending the effort of the Ekiti governor, the monarch stated, “I must acknowledge you specifically. What this government did for this community by resolving a matter that had lingered for over 25 years was impressive. The governor did this through due process, patience, and genuine commitment to doing what was right for Oke-Ako community. We are grateful. I am personally grateful.”

Mr Oni assured the people that he would work assiduously to unite and develop the community, by partnering with all stakeholders, regardless of past grievances to lift the town out of underdevelopment to a pedestal of economic, political and social prosperity.

He said, “From this day, I am pleading to every Oke Ako indigene, regardless of which family you come from, regardless of which side of any past dispute you stood in, regardless of what happened before, to make a decision that we must forge ahead in unity. Whatever divided us in the past must be left behind. We don’t have the luxury of carrying old grievances into a new era.”

READ ALSO: Abducted Ekiti church worshippers freed after 67 days in captivity

The Commissioner for Chieftaincy and Home Affairs in Ekiti State, Ojo Atibioke, explained that the process that produced the new monarch was undertaken with full fidelity to the state Chiefs Law, and in compliance with the culture, customs and traditions of Oke Ako town.

Mr Atibioke stated, “Today belongs not only to the new Oba, but to all the indigenes of Oke Ako. A vacant throne creates a gap in the life of a community. A filled throne creates opportunities. The opportunity before Oke Ako now is to put years of uncertainty behind and build a future in which the palace becomes the centre of unity and development.”

World.title: UK Latest Travel Advisory: Mbah’s security investment positionong Enugu globally, By Chikwado Odo
World.content:

This is exactly what we’re witnessing in Enugu under the intellectually guided administration of Dr Peter Ndubuisi Mbah, where genuine applause for his intentional, standard and verifiable massive development and economic indices transcend beyond the next election to the next generation.

When Governor Mbah assumed office 29 May 2023, he inherited an Enugu with enormous economic potential and a proud developmental history, but also faced serious security and economic challenges that demanded decisive and innovative leadership systems confront.

And because he understood clearly that for his ambitious development visions to succeed, he needs to create an environment that will be economically friendly, allow free movement of people and goods, establish strong confidence, trust and stability for investors to thrive in a business ecosystem of strong and responsive ans smart security network.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He therefore placed security at the epicentre of his administration’s economic strategy while simultaneously pursuing reforms that could unlock Enugu’s productive trajectory.

The decisive restoration of normal economic and social activities, especially the effective end of the prolonged sit at home order, remained one of the most distinctive outcomes of this unusual leadership approach of His Excellency.

The significance of this achievement is underscored by the latest UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office travel advisory, updated on 20 August 2026.

That Enugu is not among the Nigerian areas currently subjected to the UK’s major against all travel or against all but essential travel restrictions totaling thirty states and FCT, represents a direct function and reflection of how this administration has projected and focused the image of our dear Enugu State on the economic prosperity searchlights and map of of the world.

Although the UK may not have formally published a *safest states ranking*, but Enugu’s favourable position within the advisory represents an important international signal of its improved security environment.

It’s therefore worthy to highlight that with the UK latest report, together with different verifiable and practical data already on ground from reputable organisations, it’s obvious that Enugu enjoys the rare status of the ‘safest state in Nigeria’.

And the economic implications are enormous. With the security substantially consolidated and strengthened under an impressive and innovative security architecture, Governor Mbah has been able to pursue massive road construction, industrial revival, aviation development, affordable CNG mass transportation, Smart Green Schools, healthcare expansion, the International Conference Centre, Enugu Air, the Enugu International Hospital and other strategic projects without the crippling uncertainty that insecurity creates.

The growing international confidence in Enugu has therefore reinforced the state’s potential and capability in attracting greater domestic and foreign direct investment, expansion tourism and hospitality, creation of massive employment, increased commercial activities and the establishment of itself as Nigeria’s most attractive destinations for business and opportunity, as recently witnessed with Enugu now surpassing Lagos in internally generated revenue (IGR).

This worthy development drive is also a reflection of Governor Mbah’s distinctive intellectual approach to governance, with a clear understanding that security is the first infrastructure of economic development.

From restoring peace to unlocking investment and transforming infrastructure, this administration is consistently repositioning Enugu from a consumption oriented economy towards a more productive, competitive and globally focused state.

The latest international security assessment is also another indication that the trajectory is changing and that Dr. Peter Ndubuisi Mbah is increasingly emerging as a global leader whose achievement has been confirmed by the superpowers of the world.

Indeed, our Tomorrow is Here in action with magnitude and direction.

World.title: Oyo govt accuses FG of intentionally excluding Makinde from federal road project launch
World.content:
The Oyo State Government has accused the federal government of deliberately excluding Governor Seyi Makinde from the launching of the reconstruction and dualisation of the Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode Road.

The launching was held on Monday at Idi Ayunre in Oluyole Local Government Area of Oyo State, with the state government describing the governor’s exclusion as politically motivated.

Mr Makinde is the presidential candidate of the Allied People’s Movement seeking to challenge President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 presidential election.

In a statement, the Oyo State Commissioner for Information, Dotun Oyelade, said the decision was difficult to separate from the emerging political contest ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the road project was too important to the state and the wider South-west region to be reduced to a political event.

The ceremony was attended by Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun, Minister of Works Dave Umahi, the APC governorship candidate in Oyo State, Sarafadeen Alli, and the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Rashidi Ladoja.

Mr Oyelade particularly rejected the explanation that Mr Makinde was not invited because he was on leave.

According to him, the state which has an acting governor in place, could have represented at the event, if it was invited.

He described the development as a “political jamboree” and said the Makinde administration would not be distracted by it.

“The course of 2027 is set, and no level of indecorum or desperation from whatever quarters will hold back the will of the people,” Mr Oyelade said.

The Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode Road is an important route connecting Oyo and Ogun states and providing a major link across the South-West.

The planned reconstruction and dualisation is expected to improve movement along the corridor, which is used by commuters and businesses travelling between the two states and other parts of the region.

The controversy, however, has shifted attention from the infrastructure project to the growing political rivalry ahead of 2027.

Mr Makinde, a member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), is serving his second term as governor. The governor is running for president in the 2027 election through an alliance between the PDP and the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), and he has been officially affirmed as the presidential candidate of the APM.

However, the APC is seeking to strengthen its political foothold in the state.

The Oyo government said the people of the state remained the ultimate stakeholders and would determine its political direction through the ballot.

The government did not provide independent evidence that the governor’s exclusion was specifically ordered for political reasons, but maintained that the circumstances surrounding the flag-off raised legitimate concerns about the political undertone of the event.

World.title: Sultan Sa’ad Abubakar III at 70: The authority of restraint, By Samuel Aruwan
World.content:
There are leaders who enter a room determined to be heard, and there are leaders whose presence settles the room before they have spoken. His Eminence, the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammadu Sa’ad Abubakar III, belongs to the latter tradition. His authority has never depended on noise. It rests on composure, judgement and the difficult discipline of knowing when a word will heal, when it must warn, and when silence itself can carry meaning.

Today, as he turns seventy, Nigeria celebrates far more than a birthday. We honour a life shaped by duty: first in uniform, then on one of Africa’s most consequential traditional thrones. Born on 24 August 1956 into the royal house of the Sokoto Caliphate, he was formed by inheritance and service alike. Barewa College and the Nigerian Defence Academy prepared him for a career in which discipline was not an ornament but a daily demand. He served at home and abroad, in command and diplomatic assignments, and rose to the rank of Brigadier General.

That background matters. It explains something of the Sultan’s manner: the straight bearing, the economy of speech, the instinct for order and the refusal to panic when the national temperature rises. Yet the soldier in him has never crowded out the spiritual guide. If military service taught him command, the throne enlarged his understanding of care. He has carried both lessons together – firmness without cruelty, faith without fanaticism, and tradition without a quarrel with the modern world.

When he ascended the throne on 2 November 2006, it was in a season of grief following the tragic death of his elder brother, Sultan Muhammadu Maccido. He inherited not merely a palace, but an immense moral burden. The Sultan of Sokoto is custodian of an historic institution and spiritual leader to millions of Muslims. In a country as large, complex and diverse as Nigeria, that responsibility requires more than ceremony. It requires balance. For almost twenty years, Sultan Sa’ad Abubakar has supplied it with uncommon steadiness.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The military chapter of his life deserves more than a passing reference, because it was neither brief nor ceremonial. He entered the Nigerian Defence Academy in 1975 as a member of the 18th Regular Course and was commissioned a Second Lieutenant in 1977. He served in the Nigerian Army’s Armoured Corps, a demanding formation in which mobility, precision and disciplined judgement are essential. Over nearly three decades, he moved through field, command, liaison and diplomatic responsibilities before retiring as a Brigadier General in 2006.

His early service exposed him to the hard realities of conflict beyond Nigeria’s borders. In the early 1980s, he served with the Organisation of African Unity peacekeeping mission in Chad. Peacekeeping asks something different from ordinary soldiering. It demands the capacity to hold force in reserve, to understand local tensions, to work with soldiers of other nations and to protect a fragile political process from collapse. Long before he became known nationally as an advocate of dialogue, he had seen at close quarters what happens when dialogue fails.

He later served in a presidential security unit of the Armoured Corps and continued to rise through operational command. In 1993, he became Commanding Officer of 241 Recce Battalion in Kaduna. A reconnaissance commander must read ground, people and danger before others see them clearly. The work rewards patience, alertness and the ability to act decisively without acting rashly. These are military virtues, but they are also visible in the way the Sultan has approached moments of national tension.

From 1995 to 1999, he served as an ECOWAS military liaison officer, working within the complicated machinery of regional cooperation. He subsequently commanded 231 Tank Battalion during ECOMOG operations in Sierra Leone from 1999 to 2000. That conflict was among West Africa’s most brutal crises. Service in such an environment was not an abstraction in international affairs; it meant confronting the consequences of state failure, armed violence and the destruction of ordinary life. It helps explain why his later appeals for peace have carried the weight of experience rather than the softness of sentiment.

His final years in uniform broadened that experience further. From 2003 until 2006, he served as Nigeria’s defence adviser in Pakistan, with concurrent regional accreditation. The posting required diplomacy, discretion and an understanding of how security, religion, history and national interest intersect. It placed a Nigerian officer from Sokoto in a complex international environment and sharpened the habit of listening across cultures. By the time he was called home to ascend the throne, he had commanded soldiers, represented his country and worked inside both military and diplomatic institutions. The throne did not erase that training; it gave it a larger field of service.

Nigeria is not an easy country in which to be a religious leader. Every careless sentence can travel farther than its correction. Every grievance has merchants willing to turn it into suspicion. In such an atmosphere, the Sultan has treated words as a trust. He has consistently called Muslims to the demands of faith while speaking to the nation in the language of shared citizenship. He has shown that devotion to one’s religion need not produce hostility to another person’s faith.

His commitment to interfaith understanding is not a fashionable pose. It has been tested in moments of anger, fear and bloodshed. Again and again, he has stood for dialogue when division appeared more popular. He has reached across the Christian-Muslim divide, supported the work of inter-religious bodies, and insisted that Nigeria’s diversity is not a sentence from which we must escape, but a reality we must learn to govern with justice. This has made him a reassuring figure not only to the Muslim Ummah but also to Nigerians who do not share his faith.

There is courage in this moderation. Our public culture often mistakes restraint for timidity and courtesy for surrender. The Sultan has never confused civility with weakness. He can be measured and still be unmistakably firm. On insecurity, poverty, injustice, the failures of leadership and the moral condition of society, he has spoken with a frankness that leaves little room for convenient interpretation. He respects constituted authority, but he does not flatter it. He honours institutions, but he understands that institutions retain honour only when they serve the people.

For Northern Nigeria in particular, his voice has carried the concern of a father. He has not romanticised the region’s difficulties. He has lamented the loss of lives, the spread of fear, the decline of education and the hardship borne by ordinary families. He has reminded leaders that statistics do not bury the dead, comfort the displaced or return children to classrooms. His interventions have often brought the conversation back to the human cost of failure, the widow, the orphan, the farmer afraid to reach his field, the traveller uncertain of the road home.

This is why the Sultanate under him has remained relevant. He understands that tradition survives not by withdrawing behind palace walls, but by meeting the anxieties of the age. He has preserved the dignity of the throne while using its reach to encourage peace, learning, compassion and responsible citizenship. He speaks from an ancient seat, but he does not speak only about the past. His concern is the Nigeria before us and the Nigeria our children will inherit.

Perhaps the most striking quality of Sultan Sa’ad Abubakar’s leadership is his refusal to make himself the centre of every story. In an age of relentless self-, that is almost radical. He carries rank easily because he is not consumed by it. The splendour of office has not robbed him of humour, warmth or the capacity to listen. Those qualities explain why people of different generations, regions and convictions can approach him without feeling that they must first surrender their dignity.

At seventy, his life also offers a lesson to younger Nigerians who have come to associate leadership with display. Real authority is built slowly. It is built by preparation before opportunity arrives; by doing unglamorous work well; by keeping faith with people when there is no applause; and by accepting that high office is a heavier form of service, not a licence for excess. The Sultan’s journey from cadet to general, diplomat and royal father makes that lesson visible.

No tribute should pretend that one man can resolve all the contradictions of a nation. The value of the Sultan’s example lies elsewhere. He has shown what a leader can do with moral credibility: lower the heat, widen the space for reason, defend the vulnerable, and remind power that it is accountable. He has been a bridge at a time when bridge-building is thankless work. Bridges are stepped upon from both sides; they receive little praise for the burdens they carry. Yet without them, people remain stranded on opposite banks.

Seventy is a landmark, but it is not an ending. It is a vantage point from which a grateful nation can see the distance already travelled and pray for the road ahead. We thank Almighty God for the life of His Eminence and for the stability, wisdom and humanity he has brought to the Sultanate, the Muslim Ummah and Nigeria. We pray that God grants him sound health, renewed strength, deeper wisdom and many more years of purposeful service.

Happy seventieth birthday, Your Eminence. May your voice remain clear, your judgement sound and your days fruitful. May the throne of your forebears continue, under your stewardship, to be a shelter for the faithful, a meeting place for Nigerians and a steady light in uncertain times. Amin.

Samuel Aruwan is a postgraduate student at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria.

World.title: Shina Philips backs Nigerian football to bounce back from recent setbacks
World.content:
President of the Nigeria Pitch Awards, Shina Philips, has expressed confidence that Nigerian football will recover from its recent setbacks and regain its place among Africa’s leading football nations.

Mr Philips spoke in Abuja on Monday as the organisers of the annual Nigeria Pitch Awards announced that the 12th edition of the awards ceremony will be held on 8 September at the Ibis Hotel, Toyin Street, Ikeja, Lagos.

His comments come after a difficult period for Nigeria’s national teams, with the Super Eagles and Super Falcons recently suffering setbacks in their respective World Cup qualification campaigns.

Despite the disappointments, Mr Philips said the quality of Nigerian players competing in leagues around the world provides reason for optimism.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We have absolute confidence in our footballers who are doing well in various leagues across Europe, America, Africa, and other parts of the world,” he said.

He said the decision to proceed with the 12th edition of the awards at this time was a demonstration of the organisers’ belief in Nigerian football and its players.

“Hosting the 12th Awards Ceremony at this time is a demonstration of our faith in Nigerian football. Since 2013, when we held our maiden edition in Calabar, we have shown Nigerians that our players deserve commendations and encouragement for their selfless, patriotic contributions to the growth of our football,” Mr Philips said.

The awards ceremony was initially scheduled for earlier in the year but was postponed. Mr Philips apologised for the delay, explaining that the trophies and other logistics were already in place, but some factors forced the organisers to shift the date.

“All necessary logistics, including the award statuettes, have been in place, but the awards themselves could not be held as earlier scheduled,” he said.

Lookman, Osimhen, Nnadozie in contention

The 12th Nigeria Pitch Awards will feature 18 categories, with several Super Eagles and Super Falcons players among the nominees.

For the King of the Pitch award, Atlético de Madrid forward Ademola Lookman, Fulham defender Calvin Bassey and Galatasaray striker Victor Osimhen are the nominees.

Lookman and Osimhen are also competing for the Rashidi Yekini Award for Best Striker of the Year, alongside Anas Yusuf of Wolaita Dicha FC.

The Queen of the Pitch award will be contested by Super Falcons goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie of Brighton & Hove Albion Women, Esther Okoronkwo of AFC Toronto and Rasheedat Ajibade of Paris Saint-Germain.

Other categories include Goalkeeper, Defender, Midfielder, Team, Coach, Sportsmanship, Corporate Sponsor and Football Journalist of the Year across print, television, radio and online platforms.

Remo Stars, Rivers United and the Super Falcons are nominated for Team of the Year, while Daniel Ogunmodede, Finidi George and Justin Madugu are in contention for Coach of the Year.

READ ALSO: How Rivers Uniteds Champions League collapse exposes cracks in Nigerian football

For the State with the Best Grassroots Football Development Programme, Delta, Kwara and Lagos states are the nominees.

The Football Pitch of the Year category features the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo, the MKO Abiola Sports Arena in Abeokuta, and the Remo Stars Stadium in Remo.

Governors Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos, Dapo Abiodun of Ogun and Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom are nominated for Football Friendly Governor of the Year.

The awards ceremony is expected to bring together football administrators, players, coaches, government officials, corporate organisations and members of the media to recognise contributions to Nigerian football.

World.title: Tinubu flags off reconstruction of Ibadan–Ijebu-Ode Road, approves Abeokuta–Ibadan dualisation
World.content:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has flagged off the reconstruction and dualisation of the 58-kilometre Ibadan–Ijebu-Ode Road linking Oyo and Ogun states, while approving the immediate reconstruction and dualisation of the Abeokuta–Ibadan Road.

The projects, according to the President, are part of the Federal Government’s efforts to strengthen transportation networks, deepen economic integration and address critical infrastructure deficits across the South-West.

Speaking at the flag-off ceremony held at the open field of Legacy Estate, Idi-Ape, Ibadan, President Tinubu, who was represented by Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, said the projects demonstrated his administration’s commitment to improving strategic economic corridors and delivering infrastructure that directly impacts the lives of Nigerians.

President Tinubu described the Ibadan–Ijebu-Ode corridor as a major economic artery connecting Ibadan, Ijebu-Ode and the Lekki economic axis, with links to other parts of the South-West and the country.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the occasion demonstrated what purposeful leadership could accomplish when political will was driven by genuine concern for the welfare and prosperity of the people.

According to him, the flag-off was more than the commencement of another road project, but “a decisive statement that no critical infrastructure deficit will be ignored and no strategic economic corridor will be allowed to stand in the way of our collective prosperity.”

“The Ibadan–Ijebu-Ode Road is too important to Oyo State, Ogun State, Lagos and, indeed, the entire Nigeria to be left unattended to.

“Today, the Renewed Hope Agenda moves beyond promises into practical action through a project that will improve mobility, strengthen commerce and create new possibilities for our people,” he said.

The President noted that improved road infrastructure would boost commerce, enhance productivity, reduce transportation costs and create employment opportunities for farmers, traders, manufacturers and other Nigerians.

He disclosed that the Ibadan–Ijebu-Ode project would involve the construction of approximately 58 kilometres of dual carriageway using continuous reinforced concrete pavement to ensure durability, safety and long-term value.

President Tinubu said the contractor had assured the government that the project would be completed in less than 24 months, charging the company to mobilise fully to site, adhere strictly to approved specifications and deliver the project within the agreed timeframe.

He also appealed to host communities to cooperate with the Federal Ministry of Works, contractors and relevant government agencies to ensure the smooth execution of the project.

He warned against encroachment, disruption and unreasonable demands that could delay construction, stressing that the success of the project depended on the cooperation of all stakeholders.

According to him, the real value of the road would be measured by its impact on Nigerians, particularly through improved movement of agricultural produce from farms to markets, easier transportation of raw materials and finished goods, reduced travel time and better access to jobs, education and healthcare.

President Tinubu added that the approval for the reconstruction and dualisation of the Abeokuta–Ibadan Road would further improve connectivity between the two major cities and stimulate economic activities across Ogun and Oyo states.

The Minister of Works, Dave Umahi, disclosed that President Tinubu had directed the immediate reconstruction and dualisation of the 70-kilometre Ibadan–Abeokuta Road, noting that the procurement process was already ongoing.

Umahi said Oyo State currently had 17 major road projects out of the 47 Federal Government projects being executed across the South-West.

He added that Ogun and Ondo states had a combined 82-kilometre stretch of the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway, which, he said, would provide access to the biggest seaport currently being developed in Ogun State.

While highlighting some of the projects being executed by the Federal Government in the South-West, the Minister listed the 1,068-kilometre Badagry–Sokoto Road, noting that 258 kilometres had already been dualised.

He also mentioned the 56-kilometre Oyo–Ogbomoso Road, which he said was 80 per cent completed, as well as the 34-kilometre Oyo–Ibadan Road, which was abandoned but had been resuscitated by the present administration.

Umahi described JRB, the contractor handling the Ibadan–Ijebu-Ode Road, as one of the best-equipped indigenous contractors in the country, with a record of executing quality projects across Nigeria.

He called on the people of the affected communities to support the contractor and ensure the timely completion of the project.

Also speaking, the Chairman, Senate Committee on Works, Senator Allwell Onyesoh, said the road was conceived during the administration of the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo in 1965 to link the people of Ibadan and Ijebu.

He noted that President Tinubu’s decision to reconstruct and modernise the road would make it more functional, reduce travel time and minimise accidents along the corridor.

The member representing Ijebu North, Ijebu East and Ogun Waterside Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Hon. Joseph Adegbesan, said he moved the motion for the reconstruction of the road because of its importance to the socio-economic development of Ogun and Oyo states.

He said the road provided critical access to markets, farmlands and educational institutions, expressing appreciation to President Tinubu for responding to the demands of the people by awarding the contract for its reconstruction.

The Chairman, House Committee on Works, Hon. Akin Alabi, said the project would bring relief to the people after many years of travelling on the deplorable road.

He assured that the people would cooperate with the Federal Government and the contractor to ensure the timely completion of the project.

In his goodwill message, the Ebumawe of Ago-Iwoye, Oba Rasak Adenugba, recalled the deplorable condition of the road and its negative impact on the socio-economic development of communities along the corridor.

He said its reconstruction would revive commercial activities, improve connectivity and reduce accidents, calling on the people to support and cooperate with the contractor for the speedy completion of the project.

The Olubadan of Ibadan, Oba Rashid Ladoja, noted that the poor condition of the road had created security challenges, including making parts of the corridor vulnerable to criminal activities.

He expressed optimism that the reconstruction would help reduce incidents of banditry and kidnapping, while further strengthening the existing peaceful relationship between the people of Ibadan and Ijebu.

Oba Ladoja urged the contractor to work diligently towards the speedy completion of the project for the benefit of the people.

The Ibadan–Ijebu-Ode Road project was awarded on 5 May 2026, and commenced on 11 July 2026. It is expected to be completed by 10 June 2029.

World.title: Osun gets new police commissioner
World.content:
The Nigeria Police Force has redeployed Osun State’s Commissioner of Police Ibrahim Gotan from the state Command and appointed Ibrahim Zungura to replace him.

The development comes less than two weeks after the conclusion of the Osun governorship election and months after Mr Gotan came under sustained criticism from political actors and civil society groups over allegations that the state police command was not impartial in handling politically sensitive matters ahead of the 15 August poll.

The new development was confirmed to PREMIUM TIMES by the Osun State Police spokesperson, Abiodun Ojelabi, who said the command would issue a statement containing details of the new commissioner’s deployment and Mr Gotan’s transfer.

“Yes, but we will drop a press release before the night,” the spokesperson said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

PREMIUM TIMES reported that Mr Zungura was among the 17 Deputy Commissioners of Police promoted to the rank of Commissioner of Police by the Police Service Commission (PSC) in July.

The Nigeria Police Force later listed him among senior officers affected by its nationwide postings. Before the latest development, he was listed as Commissioner of Police in charge of Training and Courses at the Police Academy, Kano in early August.

His appointment places him at the helm of the Osun State Command at a time when the state is still dealing with the security fallout of the 15 August governorship election, including disputes over local government control and alleged political violence.

How Gotan became a subject of controversy

Mr Gotan’s tenure in Osun had become increasingly controversial in the months leading up to the election.

Governor Ademola Adeleke’s administration had repeatedly criticised the police command, accusing it of partisan conduct and demanding that the Inspector-General of Police intervene.

In January, the state government accused the command of what it described as “unacceptable partisan conduct” over the arrest and continued detention of one of the governor’s aides.

The criticism intensified in June when Accord Party lawmakers accused Mr Gotan of failing to adequately respond to politically motivated attacks against members of the ruling party. A coalition of civil society groups also demanded his redeployment, alleging that his continued presence could undermine confidence in the policing of the election.

The police, however, did not publicly accept the allegations of partisanship against Mr Gotan.

Instead, the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, later explained that the decision to remove Mr Gotan from election command followed complaints from political stakeholders who said they had lost confidence in his neutrality.

Mr Disu said the decision was not a disciplinary action against Mr Gotan but was taken to restore confidence in the command ahead of the election.

Police earlier deployed an election CP

On 31 July, PREMIUM TIMES reported Nigeria Police Force announced the deployment of Commissioner of Police Samuel Erale to Osun as the CP Elections, specifically to coordinate security operations for the August 15 governorship poll.

At the time, however, the Force clarifiedthat Mr Gotan remained the substantive Commissioner of Police in Osun and would continue to oversee routine policing activities while providing administrative and operational support to Mr Erale.

The arrangement was presented by the police as part of its strategy to ensure a peaceful and credible election.

Mr Erale was tasked with coordinating election security across the state in collaboration with other security agencies and stakeholders, while officers deployed for the election were directed to remain professional, neutral and compliant with the Code of Conduct for Security Personnel on Electoral Duty.

The arrangement was later explained by Mr Disu as an attempt to restore confidence in the police command after political parties complained about Mr Gotan’s neutrality.

Mr Erale subsequently became the face of the Nigerian police in the election security in Osun, with the police deploying thousands of personnel across the state’s 30 local government areas and polling units. On election day, he said the security situation was calm and that officers were moving across the state to monitor the exercise.

Gotan not to return after election

The latest deployment of new CP to Osun State changes the arrangement the police announced before the election.

The Force initially said Mr Gotan would remain in charge of the Osun Command and would continue routine policing after the election, but he has now been moved out of the command and replaced with Mr Zungura.

The development means that the substantive leadership of the Osun Police Command has changed after the election rather than returning to the arrangement that existed before the poll.

It also marks the latest chapter in a recurring pattern in Osun, where changes in police leadership have become closely associated with concerns about the neutrality of security agencies during governorship elections.

READ ALSO: Osun constitutes committee to disburse N500m fund to election violence victims

Redeployment of CP not the first ahead of Osun election

Mr Gotan’s redeployment is not the first time the police have changed the leadership of the Osun Command around a governorship election.

Ahead of the 2022 governorship election, then Commissioner of Police Olawale Olokode was also temporarily removed from the state command after coming under criticism over the handling of security matters.

Civil society groups and supporters of the then Minister of Interior, Rauf Aregbesola, had demanded Mr Olokode’s removal following attacks on campaign offices and allegations that the command was not acting impartially. The Nigeria Union of Journalists also demanded his redeployment after a journalist was shot by police officers while covering a protest in Osogbo.

The then Inspector-General of Police, Usman Alkali, subsequently ordered Mr Olokode’s temporary redeployment to Force Headquarters in Abuja until the conclusion of the election. CP Julius Alawari was deployed to Osun to oversee the command during the election period.

World.title: Otedola buys 95.7 million First HoldCo shares, moves stake up 27.7%
World.content:
Femi Otedola, the chairman of First HoldCo Plc, acquired 95.7 million new shares in the banking group, taking his stake in the company to 27.70 per cent.

In a regulatory filing signed by the group’s Company Secretary, Abiola Baruwa, on Monday, Mr Otedola purchased 95,699,240 additional shares at N131.48 per share, valued at N12.58 billion.

The additional share purchase represents 0.21 per cent of the company’s outstanding shares and was made through Calvados Global Services Limited.

After the purchase, Mr Otedola now holds about 12.14 billion shares in the financial institution, representing 27.70 per cent of the company’s outstanding shares.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Based on the financial institution’s opening price of N129.95 on Monday at the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX), the First HoldCo chair’s total shareholding in the company is valued at about N1.58 trillion.

The new share acquisition is another purchase by Mr Otedola in recent times, as the businessman has been increasing his investment in the financial institution.

In recent weeks, the tycoon has cumulatively purchased over 2.16 billion shares of the lender. The latest share purchase is the third time in August that Mr Otedola has increased his stake in the financial services group, following his acquisitions of 147.7 million and 138 million shares on 17 August and 7 August, respectively.

Also, on 30 July, Mr Otedola increased his stake in the financial services group by acquiring an additional 1.78 billion shares at N124.90 per share, valued at about N222.2 billion.

The steady accumulation of shares has further strengthened Mr Otedola’s position as First HoldCo’s largest shareholder, overtaking RC Investment, the bridge holder that previously held the largest stake in the company at about 22.94 per cent.

RC Investment emerged in July 2025 as the trustee for 10.4 billion shares simultaneously offloaded by Oba Otudeko and Oye Hassan-Odukale, who were among First HoldCo’s major shareholders at the time, in a single-day transaction.
