World.title: Iraq, Qatar provide oil for loading inside Hormuz via bids
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Trade sources reported on Monday that Iraq’s national oil marketer, SOMO, and QatarEnergy are presenting crude oil through unusual bids that mandate purchasers to load cargoes within the Strait of Hormuz.

SOMO announced that it is offering Basrah Medium and Basrah Heavy crude for loading in September from either the Basrah oil port or a single point mooring, along with the necessary supporting facilities, as reported by Reuters.

QatarEnergy provided free-on-board oil loading at al-Shaheen, Qatar Marine, and Qatar Land ports in September and October.

Earlier, SOMO provided substantial discounts on Basrah crude in August to entice customers to load shipments from the Strait of Hormuz.

SOMO asked potential term purchasers to designate contractual volumes of Basrah Medium or Basrah Heavy crude for complimentary onboard delivery from the Basrah Oil Terminal or other port-related infrastructure.

Iraq’s oil marketer provided discounts ranging between $25 and $27 per barrel on Basrah Medium, according to the loading period. It provided discounts of $27.80 to $29.80 a barrel for Basrah Heavy.

Maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz decreased due to ongoing military operations in the region and heightened shipping security risks.

The significant price reduction aims to compensate for rising maritime insurance costs and freight expenses by transferring transit risk to purchasers.

World.title: Iraq to introduce new banknotes with three zeros removed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq intends to remove three zeros from its currency to modernize financial transactions, reduce physical cash circulation, and return stockpiled funds to the official banking system.

Under the suggestion, a 25,000-Iraqi dinar note would become 25 Iraqi dinars, but the currency’s purchasing power and true financial value would stay unaffected.

According to Jamal Kocher, a Kurdish member of the Iraqi parliament’s finance committee, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has asked for the removal of zeros from invoices.

Kocher told The New Region that if the plan is implemented, 1,000 Iraqi dinars would be converted to one dinar, while 25,000 dinars would be equivalent to 25 dinars.

Earlier in August, Communications Minister Mustafa Sanad acknowledged the plan to eliminate the zeros and modify the currency.

The redenomination strategy aims to bring undeclared cash, estimated to be between 8 and 10 trillion Iraqi dinars that are currently held outside banks, back into official channels. This initiative seeks to combat crime, corruption, and money laundering.

According to the idea, everyday prices, incomes, and savings will alter correspondingly, resulting in a direct mathematical shift rather than a change in actual wealth.

Iraq has sought printing partners in the United Kingdom and Australia, as well as its traditional suppliers in France and Germany, to create an estimated 7.5 billion new banknotes.

While government officials such as the Communications Minister and Finance Committee members have emphasized the importance of an official implementation date, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) has yet to present a formal draft bill to parliament.

World.title: Iraq to raise oil exports via Turkey’s Ceyhan to 750,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil announced on Sunday a proposal to increase oil exports through the Turkish port of Ceyhan to 750,000 barrels per day by using tanker trucks to transport crude oil from southern oilfields.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the plan includes increasing exports through southern ports.

Iraq and Turkey recently inked a one-year short-term deal to continue operations through the critical Iraq-Turkey oil pipeline.

The agreement, reached in Ankara following discussions between Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar and Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair, guarantees the ongoing transportation of at least 750,000 barrels of Iraqi crude oil per day to the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Turkey’s state-owned crude oil and natural gas pipeline corporation (BOTAS) signed an agreement with Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) and the North Oil Company (NOC).

The new deal is now valid for 12 months until both countries develop a new, long-term legislative framework.

The previous agreement, which was reached in 1973, officially expired on July 27.

The short extension of the deal is crucial for Iraq’s revenue from oil exports, as Baghdad seeks alternative export routes to mitigate risks linked to the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Eto’o urges support for embattled FIFA president Infantino
World.content:
Paris – Former Cameroon star Samuel Eto’o has thrown his support behind beleaguered FIFA president Gianni Infantino, saying he “hasn’t done anything wrong” despite facing mounting pressure to step down over a controversial World Cup sell-off plan.

Infantino has come under intense scrutiny since the collapse of a proposal to secure private investment in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup.

UEFA, which oversees European football, has threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions with several continental and national federations also withdrawing their support for Infantino.

However, Eto’o, president of the Cameroonian football federation, dismissed criticism of Infantino’s leadership, suggesting the backlash was driven largely by political manoeuvring ahead of FIFA’s presidential election next year.

“I don’t think that President Gianni Infantino has done anything wrong,” the former Barcelona, Inter Milan and Chelsea striker told CNN.

“I think the timing of all of that is because there’s an election coming out.”

Infantino’s plan, which would reportedly have distributed substantial funding to FIFA’s 211 member associations, faced strong opposition from several confederations and was ultimately abandoned.

The FIFA president remains under pressure, with the possibility of a no-confidence vote being triggered. UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF — which governs North and Central America and the Caribbean — have all voiced concerns over FIFA’s direction in recent weeks.

But the Confederation of African Football (CAF) earlier this month “unanimously reconfirmed its support” for Infantino, and Eto’o’s backing is aligned with that position.

“President Gianni Infantino has changed football,” said Eto’o, urging fellow African countries to support the Swiss official.

“He’s given opportunities to nations that didn’t have those opportunities to take part in the most beautiful tournament, the World Cup. He enabled smaller nations to get seats at these competitions.

“He has helped our continent. He’s helped our federations to develop much more quickly, and we need to acknowledge that. We need to accept and recognise what he’s done, and we should support him for everything he’s done up to now.”

World.title: Trump claims Iran ‘collapsing’ as US threatens ‘economic D-Day’
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump said Monday that Iran was “collapsing” as Washington prepared to announce the details of a new economic pressure campaign that Tehran has derided as an admission of defeat.

Almost six months into their war, the two sides are locked in a stalemate, with peace talks stalled, Iran keeping the key Strait of Hormuz shut and Washington persisting with a naval counter-blockade of Iran.

Under political pressure at home over the economic impacts of the conflict, Trump has pivoted away from military action to economic levers.

“IRAN IS COMPLETELY COLLAPSING!!!” the president posted Monday in his trademark all-caps style on his social media platform Truth Social.

His remarks came hours after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in a column for the Financial Times, declared that an “economic D-Day” had begun against Tehran and warned that any country that continued to enable the Islamic republic would become a “global pariah”.

Bessent also claimed on X that the US had “dismantled Iran’s military capabilities, destroyed nearly 100 percent of its military factories, and buried its nuclear programme”.

Iran responded with defiance, saying the latest US measures were an admission of military defeat, and it warned countries against aiding Washington.

Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi posted on X that the US turn to financial warfare proved Bessent’s claims false.

“Your narrative doesn’t add up,” Gharibabadi said, asking why, if Washington had achieved its goals, “there is a need for ‘the largest financial invasion in history’ and the mobilisation of ‘all institutions and powers’ of the United States!

“Is this a victory or an admission of America’s defeat?”

The US and Israel linked the launch of their war in February to Iran’s nuclear programme, but the focus since the early days of fighting has been on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital route for global oil and gas supplies.

Tehran continues to blockade the strait, which it did not restrict before the war, driving up global inflation and heaping domestic pressure on Trump ahead of mid-term elections in November.

– Oil exports plunge –

Bessent was due to set out details of the US plan on Monday, but it is unclear how much more economic pressure Washington can put on Tehran.

The US naval blockade of Iran has seen its oil exports via the Strait of Hormuz fall from two million barrels a day pre-war to just 0.4 million by mid-August, according to maritime tracker Kpler.

Meanwhile, the country has been under crushing international sanctions for decades, with a brief period of easing under a 2015 nuclear deal that Trump later ripped up as part of a “maximum pressure” campaign.

The Islamic republic has weathered those efforts and, before the war, continued to export millions of barrels of oil, mostly to China, and evade sanctions through complex international financial networks.

Bessent and Trump have both warned countries against helping Iran, signalling a shift in their focus, with the Treasury secretary’s FT column dwelling on nations who “appease” and “enable” Iran.

Tehran responded on Monday by warning countries not to cooperate with the US efforts. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said taking part would “definitely have its own consequences”.

For ordinary Iranians, the standoff is likely to bring only more economic pain after years of rampant inflation, which in December and January fuelled massive anti-government protests.

Sarah Hassanbeigi, a 32-year-old pharmacist in Tehran, put it simply: “It’s really very difficult. I don’t think people can really take this much longer.”

On Sunday, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian admitted that Iran faced “many problems in society”.

“We are striving with all our hearts to overcome inflation, livelihood problems, unemployment, and to secure the future of the people, so that they can live with dignity and pride,” Pezeshkian said.

– Delegation from Pakistan –

Last week, the Iranian president, considered a relative moderate, said Tehran should “bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity”.

That followed supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei appointing hardliners to key security positions.

Hassanbeigi said she wanted peace. “Naturally, negotiations mean that both sides have to compromise. My personal opinion is that Iran should compromise now,” she told AFP.

Throughout the war, diplomatic efforts, pushed on by mediators, have sought a negotiated end to the conflict.

On Monday, Pakistan’s army chief was expected in Iran. Islamabad was a leading mediator in talks that helped secure an April ceasefire that later fell apart.

Omani Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi was also due in Iran on Tuesday, as Muscat and Tehran seek a deal on regulating passage through Hormuz.

World.title: Liverpool must improve on ‘unacceptable’ season, says Van Dijk
World.content:
Liverpool – Virgil van Dijk said Liverpool “need to show a reaction” from a bitterly disappointing season that cost Arne Slot his job as manager, but called for patience with new boss Andoni Iraola.

The Reds needed a 99th-minute equaliser from the penalty spot by Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue a 2-2 draw at Newcastle on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

Slot guided Liverpool to glory and a 20th league title in his debut campaign in 2024/25, but paid the price for finishing fifth last season when he was dismissed in May.

Many of the same flaws were in evidence in Iraola’s first outing at St James’ Park as Newcastle sliced open the Liverpool defence on the counter-attack.

But they twice came from behind to avoid a losing start to the new season.

“It’s absolutely normal in any type of profession, work, whatever you do, if you come in new and you have new plans and new ideas, then it takes a bit of time with new players,” said Van Dijk.

“It’s down to us to do it as soon as we can, as soon as possible, because we want to improve, we want to win, we want to be better. That’s what we are going to try to do.

“We need to show a reaction from last year, that we are much better than last year, because this was very unacceptable.”

Iraola has not been aided by a lack of new arrivals in the transfer market.

Despite the departure of club legend Mohamed Salah and a long-term injury to Hugo Ekitike, Liverpool have only added Spanish winger Victor Munoz in attacking areas as well as defenders Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo.

Paris Saint-Germain’s two-time Champions League winner Bradley Barcola has been linked with a move to Anfield, while two bids for Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh have reportedly been turned down.

“Everyone wants to see quality arrive regardless and I fully trust the club and the board to make the right decisions,” Van Dijk added.

“That’s the only thing I can say, so let’s see what we are going to do.”

World.title: Iraq suggests a security council involving Iran, Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has officially suggested forming a joint security coordination council with Iran and Saudi Arabia to address what it calls a severe crisis of trust between the two regional powers.

The Security Affairs Adviser to the Prime Minister of Iraq, Qasim al-Araji, put forward the diplomatic initiative on behalf of Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government to stabilize the region where Iraq strives to manage its own turbulent security climate.

Baghdad clearly planned the initiative to reconcile serious tensions between Riyadh and Tehran.

Tensions rose as Saudi Arabia intercepted multiple drones aimed at its oil facilities and capital. Riyadh denounced Iran-backed militias that operate from inside Iraq.

The idea comes during a very unstable period, including recent US-Saudi joint airstrikes targeting Popular Mobilization Forces’ (PMF) sites in Iraq and leading to serious criticism from Baghdad for sovereignty violations.

Baghdad is also pressuring Tehran for waivers for oil tankers from Iran’s navigation restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

Additionally, al-Araji underlined Iraq’s transition to ultimate domestic sovereignty.

With the scheduled withdrawal of the US-led international coalition forces from Iraq, Baghdad is adopting a strategy to put all armed factions and weaponry under strict state supervision, consolidating the country’s ultimate authority over war and peace choices.

Neither Saudi Arabia nor Iran has released a formal public response to the Iraqi initiative.

World.title: Iraq foreign reserves decline 11.6% to $86.17B in June 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Official financial statements from the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) show that Iraq’s foreign exchange reserves declined to $86.175 billion at the end of June 2026, marking a decrease of $11.257 billion (-11.6%) compared to the $97.432 billion recorded at the close of 2025.

According to reserve records published on Monday, August 24, 2026, the contraction followed an early-year peak above $102 billion before downward momentum set in through the second quarter.

Monthly Reserve Trajectory (H1 2026)

End of 2025 Baseline: $97.432 billion

January 2026: $101.082 billion

February 2026 (Peak): $102.131 billion

March 2026: $100.341 billion

April 2026: $97.809 billion

May 2026: $93.673 billion

June 2026:$86.175 billion(Month-over-month drop of $7.498 billion)

The overall drop reduced the local currency value of the total portfolio from 126.661 trillion IQD at the end of 2025 to 112.027 trillion IQD by June 30, 2026—a net decline of 14.634 trillion IQD (-11.6%).

Reserve Component End of 2025 (IQD) End of June 2026 (IQD) Net Change Change (%) Investments & Securities 93.266 Trillion 81.998 Trillion -11.268 Trillion -12.1% Monetary Gold Reserves 31.488 Trillion 29.415 Trillion -2.073 Trillion -6.6% Cash Vault Holdings 1.907 Trillion 0.614 Trillion -1.293 Trillion -67.8% Total Equivalent Value 126.661 Trillion 112.027 Trillion -14.634 Trillion -11.6%

The reserve reduction aligns with broader fiscal pressures in the first half of 2026, during which lower oil revenues widened the state budget deficit and prompted the central bank to meet elevated domestic foreign currency demand.

While liquid investment instruments fell by 11.268 trillion IQD to absorb trade financing and foreign wire settlements, cash assets held in central bank vaults rebounded moderately in June (up to 614 billion IQD from 366 billion IQD in May), even as overall foreign exchange reserves adjusted downward to $86.175 billion.

World.title: 3 Bambiha members deported from Malaysia
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a major operation against the Bambiha criminal network, Indian agencies have executed a coordinated crackdown on its key overseas operatives, deporting three of its members from Malaysia who were ordering hits and carrying out extortions in India on behalf of the group's kingpin Lucky Patial.

Announced by Union home minister Amit Shah on X Monday, the high-profile action targeted Jaspreet Singh (alias Jas Behbal) of Faridkot, alongside Ajay Singh (alias Ajay Malaysia) and Pawandeep Singh, both from Rajasthan's Sri Ganganagar district. Shah posted that Indian agencies had got the three absconding gangsters apprehended in Malaysia and deported to India.

"The fugitives....are linked to the Bambiha gang and are accused of multiple crimes, including extortion, cross-border arms and narco-trafficking, and a foiled grenade attack in Ludhiana...our agencies have facilitated the deportation of 51 hardened criminals in 2026 alone."

World.title: Showcase India's strengths to woo tourists: PM Modi
World.content:
PM Narendra Modi

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi on Monday asked young diplomats to showcase India's civilisational, cultural and geographical strengths to make it a more attractive global tourism destination.Talking to officer trainees of the 2025 batch of Indian Foreign Service, he asked them to serve as catalytic agents for the country's economic engagement with the world.Stressing the importance of strengthening the digital presence of missions, he said a website is often the first gateway through which people interact with an institution and suggested leveraging the "Bharat ko Janiye" Quiz to generate greater interest in India among young people across the world and encouraged the use of AI to make initiatives engaging.

World.title: In a first, Census 2027 will not record data on begging
World.content:
Census 2027 drops separate âbeggars and vagrantsâ category, adds natural calamities as migration reason

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a departure from previous exercises, Census 2027 will not record data on begging separately, with the questionnaire having omitted the category 'beggars and vagrants etc' from the list of 'non-economic activity'. This, as per sources, is due to the very less return in this category in the last census; just around 3.8 lakh non-workers and marginal workers declared themselves as 'beggars and vagrants' in Census 2011.Another key change in is the inclusion of 'natural calamities' as a 'reason for migration', in addition to work, business, education, marriage, moved after birth, moved with household and 'any other'.While the 2011 census and earlier had listed 'beggars and vagrants etc' as marginal and non-workers engaged in 'non-economic activity' - in addition to students, household duties, dependents, pensioners, rentiers and others - they will now be counted among 'others'; as a result, the number of beggars in the country or their classification by age, religion, state/UT, educational status etc will no longer figure in census tables.Sources said the count of 'beggars and vagrants' returned by previous census exercises was not considered reliable, as many respondents in this category were reluctant to return themselves as such due to associated social stigma. "Census rules require the enumerator to record the occupation/non-economic activity as declared by the respondent," an officer said. The count of non-worker beggars/vagrants was thus recorded at around 3.8 lakh in Census 2011, 6.3 lakh in Census 2001 and around 5.4 lakh in Census 1991.As for the new census fields 'father's particulars' and 'mother's particulars' - which will capture date and place of their birth as well as religion - sources said they need to be filled only where the mother and father are not listed in the same household or are no longer alive. The enumeration form already records the religion and date and place of birth of each member of the census household, including parents.Sources told TOI that some of the trends that may emerge from recording religion of both parents include generation-wise prevalence of inter-faith marriages and history of religious conversion. Also, date and place of birth of parents will give the aggregate data on how many Indians fulfil citizenship criteria as per Citizenship Act.While the latest questionnaire seeks details like mobile number, Aadhaar, voter ID and Indian passport number, where "available", technically requiring every individual having these documents to share their number, sources said the enumerators have been trained to only persuade the respondents to do so, by assuring them that all individual data will remain confidential. If the respondent is still reluctant, the enumerator shall leave these fields empty."Even blank fields will enable the census team to cull out data on which of the documents - Aadhaar, voter ID and passport number - respondents are most reluctant to share due to privacy concerns," an official told TOI.

World.title: Repeated trips of Turkish military transport planes to Pak between Aug 19 & 21 raise eyebrows in India
World.content:
NEW DELHI: An unusual increase in Turkish military transport flights to Pakistan in the last few days has raised hackles in Indian defence circles.

Open-source flight trackers noted a 60-hour surge of Turkish military transport flights, including Turkish C-130 Hercules and A400M aircraft (such as one with call sign TUAF526), landing at Pakistani air bases like Nur Khan, Masroor, and Murid between August 19 and 21.

There is speculation in defence circles that the flights may have carried Turkish military hardware, including unmanned aerial systems (drones) and air-defence equipment like Baykar (next-generation kamikaze UAV K2) and Asisguard systems (drone systems) to Pakistan. The aircraft movements were seen soon after after the signing of the tripartite Mecca Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia on Aug 7.

The agreement establishes a collective defence pact, stating that an armed attack against any one of the three member states will be considered an attack against all of them.

However, neither Pakistan nor Turkey has officially confirmed the precise nature or cargo of these transport operations.

With Turkish aircraft landing in Pakistan, questions are being raised in defence circles whether Pakistan is gearing up for another conflict with India.





Before Operation Sindoor in May last year, China and Turkey had allegedly supplied Pakistan with advanced military hardware, including Chinese PL-15 air-to-air missiles and HQ-9 air defence systems, and Turkish-origin Bayraktar (Yiha) and Asisguard Songar kamikaze drones. They also provided real-time battlefield data and tactical support.

During the four-day conflict last year, the Indian armed forces tackled these attacks using their multilayered air defence grid and integrated command and control strategy, successfully intercepting all incoming aerial threats before reaching critical military or civilian infrastructure.

The Indian forces deployed indigenous technology and advanced anti-access frameworks to crush the Pakistan defence network and also thwarted its offensive attacks. The IAF used long-range capabilities of Russian-acquired S-400 Triumf air defence system and indigenous Akash-NG missiles to thwart missile and UAV attacks. The IAF also used the S-400 to shoot down a high-value Pakistani Saab 2000 Erieye AEW&C surveillance aircraft from around 314 km away â which stands as one of the longest-range combat surface-to-air missile engagements in military history.

World.title: 'Failure of judicial system': SC on 45-year-old case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: It took a lower court 22 years to complete trial in a double murder case and another 22 years for Jharkhand high court to decide the appeal, and during the long proceedings, five of six accused died and the sole surviving bed-ridden convict in his 70s is fighting a legal battle in Supreme Court from jail.

Terming the inordinate delay in deciding the case a failure of the judicial system, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran suspended the sentence of the convict and allowed him to come out of jail on bail. It also decided to examine the reason why the trial court and HC took so long in deciding the case of double murder, which took place in 1981.

The said case projects failure of the judicial system, when a crime went unpunished and the accused were put to the torture of a prolonged trial of 22 years and then after conviction, the appeal filed having been dismissed after yet another two decades and two years, SC said.

Advocate Fauzia Shakil, appearing for the convict, submitted that the petitioner will suffer grave prejudice and irreparable loss if bail is not granted to him inasmuch as there cannot be any adequate compensation for his prolonged incarceration in the event of his eventual acquittal by SC.

âDespite the horrendous crime of a double murder, we cannot close our eyes to the ordeal suffered by the accused in the last 45 years.





Especially noting his medical condition and the affidavit of the state that the petitioner is admitted in the hospital, though in custody, we suspend the sentence and direct that the petitioner shall be released forthwith on condition of his not committing any crime when on bail and on his personal surety,â it said.

âIt is very disturbing to note that although the incident is of the year 1981 yet the judgement and order passed by the trial court holding the petitioner guilty of the alleged crime is of 2002.

We fail to understand why it took 22 years for the trial court to complete the trial... Even HC took 22 years to decide the appeal preferred by the petitioner challenging the judgement and order of conviction passed by the trial court.

This delay highlighted above is something very disturbing,â SC noted in its order.

Asked by the court to give an explanation for the delay, the registrar general of HC told the court that the delay was also caused as the accused were absconding for six years.

But the court noted that there is no explanation for the 12 years it took for the trial to be completed when the charges were framed in 1991.

âWe were concerned with pendency of the criminal appeals as pointed out in the report of HC and we hence thought it fit to permit the petitioner to implead Centre in the above matter. The learned advocate-on-record appearing for HC would serve a copy of the affidavit of compliance filed by the registrar general to the office of the attorney general/solicitor general,â the court said.

World.title: Donald Trump's volatility may have made India decline G7 presser
World.content:
âUnpredictableâ Trump behind no press conference after PM Modi meeting, govt says

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Govt justified its decision not to have a news conference after PM Modi's meeting with President Donald Trump on the margins of the G7 summit in France, with official sources citing Trump's "unpredictable behaviour" at media events that have followed his meetings with heads of state/govt, including from South Africa and Ukraine.US ambassador to India Sergio Gor had earlier created a stir with his remarks about how ministry of external affairs had called to limit media interaction to photo opportunities and opening remarks without taking questions. Despite the request from MEA, as Gor had said, Trump went on to have a 45-minute unscripted news conference at the media event. Govt sources here stressed there was no unusual demand made by the Indian side.According to Gor, while MEA wanted to bring in the media, it said, "let's not do a full news conference".The ambassadorâs disclosure of what might have been a private discussion is learned to have upset the govt. âDiscussions regarding arrangements for public appearances of leaders are normal practice ahead of any VVIP visit,â said a govt source, on condition of anonymity. âDelegations when meeting Donald Trump are wary about his unpredictable behaviour, as may be seen from his interactions with president of South Africa, Ukraine, etc.Thus, the cautious approach by India,â he added.In highlighting Trumpâs previous interactions with the presidents of Ukraine and S Africa, which devolved into televised confrontations with Trump hectoring his visitors, govt sources framed Indiaâs request as a necessary safeguard against unpredictable diplomatic settings. The standard practice for govt has been to not have unscripted joint news conferences by Modi in company of the host or visiting dignitaries.This practice, though, has been questioned by local journalists recently in countries like Norway, the Netherlands, Australia and New Zealand.MEA defended the arrangement, stating that standard diplomatic procedures for international visits are followed.

SRINAGAR: J&K State Investigation Agency (SIA) has reopened the investigation into the 1998 Wandhama massacre of 23 people as part of a wider push to probe the killings of Kashmiri Pandits during the peak of militancy in the Valley.According to sources, SIA has also started a probe into the killings of prominent Kashmiri Pandit advocate-politician Tika Lal Taploo and Justice Neelkanth Ganjoo.On Jan 25, 1998, armed terrorists entered the homes of Kashmiri Pandit families in Wandhama village of Ganderbal district and gunned down 23 people. The case still remains unresolved, but SIA sources in said it will see âsubstantial progress soonâ.Officials said SIA has undertaken a focused and comprehensive investigation into the decades-old cases to bring each of these to a logical conclusion in accordance with law. âConcerted efforts are being made to uncover the circumstances and conspiracies underlying these cases, establish credible evidence, and identify those responsible strictly on the basis of substantiated evidence and witness testimony,â said an official.Taploo, a prominent lawyer and then vice-president of J&K BJP, was shot dead near his residence in Srinagar in Sept 1989, in what among the first targeted killings of prominent Kashmiri Pandits as terrorism took roots in the Valley.Justice Ganjoo, who had sentenced JKLF founder Maqbool Bhat to death, was shot dead on Nov 4, 1989 in Srinagar.On Aug 12, SIA carried out searches at nine locations across J&K in connection with the killing of Kashmiri Pandit poet and writer Sarvanand Kaul Premi and his son by terrorists. Premi, 66, and his younger son Verinder were shot dead in Anantnag in south Kashmir on May 1, 1990, a day after they were abducted from their village.Their bodies were later found hanging from a tree. Five days later, the grief-stricken Kaul family left Kashmir, never to return.Earlier on June 29, SIA filed a 737-page chargesheet in connection with the killing of Sarla Bhat, 27, a nurse at Srinagarâs Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences. She was abducted by terrorists from the SKIMS hostel on April 18, 1990, tortured and shot dead. Her bullet-riddled body was recovered the next day.

World.title: Facing heat over power tariff hike, J&K CM Omar Abdullah says he promised free electricity, not static rates
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Chief minister Omar Abdullah Monday defended the power tariff hike in Jammu & Kashmir, saying the increase was minimal and that his govt had never promised that electricity rates would not increase.

âWhen did we say that electricity rates will not increase? We said we will provide 200 units of free electricity to the poorest people, those who need it the most,â he said.

Hitting back at political parties protesting the tariff hike, Omar said there had been only a 6% increase after a gap of four years, whereas it was much higher earlier. âThose who point fingers at me should remember that they too were in power here at some point.

During their govt, electricity rates increased by more than 14%. They did not feel at that time that this was unfair,â he said. âFour years ago, electricity rates were increased by 15%, and even then, BJP remained silent.

â

âWe are not celebrating an increase in electricity rates. This was our compulsion. As our losses in the power sector reduce, we will not need to take such steps,â the CM added.

World.title: Simultaneous polls possible in 2029, says panel chief
World.content:
Holding simultaneous elections for the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies in 2029 under the Modi government's ‘One Nation, One Election’ initiative is possible if the Constitution is amended and state governments support the move, according to P.P. Chaudhary, the chairman of the joint parliamentary panel examining the related bills.

The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024, which aim to synchronise Lok Sabha and State Assembly polls, were sent to the 31-member joint committee of Parliament headed by Mr. Chaudhary, a BJP MP from Rajasthan, following the Opposition's demand for broader scrutiny.

When asked if State assembly elections could be held alongside the 2029 Lok Sabha polls, Mr. Chaudhary said on Monday (August 24, 2026) that if the constitutional amendment is approved in Parliament by 2028, the rollout of ‘One Nation, One Election’ can begin that same year.

"Then what is the problem? If the States express their desire in 2029, we can't give the States directions to dissolve their Assembly.”

"They have to make their own decisions. It depends on the respective Chief Ministers and their Council of Ministers. If the Council of Ministers of the States decide in favour of ‘One Nation One Election’, that State elections should be held along with the Lok Sabha polls, then it is possible. It is up to them what they decide. The Indian Constitution allows that; it is permissible.”

"Under the Indian Constitution, the states are empowered to hold simultaneous polls," he told reporters at the Parliament House complex after a meeting of the panel.

The BJP leader said democracy means the will of the people, not the will of the political parties, and everyone has to see what the will of the people is.

"We have visited 10 states and interacted with a cross-section of people, and we have realised that 99 per cent of people, civil society, want simultaneous polls for Lok Sabha and State Mssemblies," he said.

Mr. Chaudhary said there may be different opinions of political parties, but the committee has to work together in the interest of the country.

"We have to work on what the people want, what the country wants. We are working with the will of the people. That is why we have invited civil society members to take their opinions," he said.

Mr. Chaudhary said that Parliament gave the panel the mandate to examine and give recommendations on the two Constitution amendment bills.

Two-thirds of members of Parliament have to support the bills for their passage.

Another government-sponsored Constitution amendment bill, the delimitation-linked women reservation bill, which also required support of two-thirds of members of Parliament, was defeated in the Lok Sabha in April.

Mr. Chaudhary said the Parliament mandated the committee to examine the legislation and fix the shortcomings, if any, and make sure that the simultaneous polls are held successfully.

He said if simultaneous elections in Lok Sabha and State assemblies are held, everyone will benefit from it and the biggest beneficiary will be the country's youth.

mr. Chaudhary also said that 30% of the time of government schools is used in poll-related work every year.

The Bills were introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2024, following which they were referred to the joint committee for examination.

The Bills were formulated after a high-level panel, headed by former President Ram Nath Kovind, recommended holding Lok Sabha, State assembly and local body elections simultaneously in a phased manner. Union Home Minister Amit Shah was also a member of the high-level panel headed by Mr. Kovind.

Following the adoption of the Constitution, elections to the Lok Sabha and all State Legislative Assemblies were conducted simultaneously from 1951 to 1967.

The first general elections to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies were held together in 1951-52, a practice that continued for three subsequent general elections in 1957, 1962, and 1967.

However, this cycle of synchronised elections was disrupted in 1968 and 1969 due to the premature dissolution of some State Legislative Assemblies.

The Fourth Lok Sabha was also dissolved prematurely in 1970, with fresh elections held in 1971. Unlike the First, Second, and Third Lok Sabha, which completed their full five-year terms, the Fifth Lok Sabha's term was extended until 1977 under Article 352 because of the declaration of Emergency.

Since then, only a few Lok Sabha terms have lasted the full five years, such as the Eighth, Tenth, Fourteenth, and Fifteenth. Others, including the Sixth, Seventh, Ninth, Eleventh, Twelfth, and Thirteenth, were dissolved early.

State Assemblies have faced similar disruptions over the years. Premature dissolutions and term extensions have become a recurring challenge.

These developments have firmly disrupted the cycle of simultaneous elections, leading to the current pattern of staggered electoral schedules across the country.

World.title: Flight diversions in Delhi-NCR, traffic jams in Jaipur as north Indian cities reel under heavy rain
World.content:
Heavy showers in many parts of north India on Monday (August 24, 2026) triggered flight diversions, waterlogging and massive traffic disruption, especially in the the Delhi-NCR region, which received the bulk of the rainfall.

Parts of Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh received rains during the day as well.

Traffic snarls were the worst in Gurugram where parents carrying children on their shoulders were seen wading through flooded roads to get to school buses and vehicles were seen stuck on waterlogged roads.

The downpour caused waterlogging in Narsinghpur, Hero Honda Chowk, Rajiv Chowk, IFFCO Chowk and several areas of old Gurugram. Vehicles were stuck in water around Rajiv Chowk, while school buses and ambulances were also caught in waterlogging on Sohna Road.

The district administration said Gurugram received 70 mm of rainfall by 1.30 p.m. Key areas including Rajiv Chowk, IFFCO Chowk, Railway Road, Sector 5, Old Delhi Road, Mehrauli Road and Basai Road were heavily affected. The Naharpur underpass was also waterlogged.

In Delhi too several key stretches, including parts of Lutyens' Delhi, Mathura Road, Connaught Place, Bhairon Marg, ITO and the Zakhira underpass, were waterlogged.

Waist-deep water, bumper-to-bumper traffic marked the day's heavy downpour, as gusty winds and showers lashed the national capital, with a few areas recording almost 67 mm of rain.

Videos shared on social media showed at least a dozen students waded through waist-deep water in Sangam Vihar. Residents in Sadar Bazar were also forced to wade through waist-deep water after rainwater accumulated in the Old Delhi area.

At least 15 flights were diverted at the Delhi airport due to inclement weather conditions. Scores of flights were delayed and some were cancelled at the Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGIA) in the national capital due to the bad weather. An official said 12 flights were diverted to Jaipur, two to Chandigarh and one to Lucknow.

Many parts of Uttar Pradesh witnessed light to moderate showers and isolated heavy downpours, disrupting normal life in urban pockets, the meteorological department said.

Monsoon remained normal across Uttar Pradesh over the past 24 hours, it said.

In Ghaziabad, heavy spells led to severe waterlogging across major roads and low-lying residential sectors, causing massive traffic congestion.

Autorickshaw overturns

In a mishap captured on cameras, an autorickshaw overturned after hitting a pothole on a waterlogged stretch and passersby rushed to rescue the passengers, who escaped with minor injuries.

According to the local MeT office, thunderstorm activity was recorded at a few places over East Uttar Pradesh and at isolated locations in West Uttar Pradesh during the last 24 hours (ending at 8:30 a.m.).

Heavy rains lashed Jaipur and other parts of eastern Rajasthan, disrupting traffic and causing waterlogging in many places.

Kherthal-Tijara in Alwar district that comes under the National Capital Region (NCR) received heavy rainfall and many areas got flooded with water.

Markets, roads, residential colonies and low-lying areas in Kishangarhbas town were also inundated due to rain.

Jaipur, Alwar, Dholpur, Karauli, Bharatpur, Sawai Madhopur, Dausa and Kherthal-Tijara districts received rains. Cars and two-wheelers were seen wading through the Moti Dungri Road in Jaipur which was completely submerged under water.

Light to moderate rain prevailed in parts of Himachal Pradesh, blocking 98 roads for vehicular traffic in the State.

As many as 98 roads were closed for vehicular traffic, while 21 power transformers and 21 drinking water supply schemes were also disrupted, the State Emergency Operation Centre (SEOC) said.

Mandi reported the highest number of road blockages at 49, followed by Kullu (28), Kangra (8), Shimla, Sirmaur, and Una (4 each), and Lahaul Spiti (1).

Light to moderate rains lashed parts of the State in the past 24 hours since Sunday evening.

Heavy rainfall, triggered by a low-pressure system, lashed most parts of Odisha, with eight places receiving more than 100-mm downpour during the past 24 hours, the IMD said.

Four places in the State recorded heavy to very heavy rainfall, while 47 places received heavy rainfall during the period till 8.30 am on Monday, it said.

The maximum rainfall of 169.4 mm was recorded at Joda in Keonjhar district, followed by Papadahandi in Nabarangpur (158.8 mm) and Paikmal in Bargarh (120 mm), the IMD said in a bulletin.

Other places that received over 100-mm rainfall include Kusumi and Jashipur in Mayurbhanj district, Jharigaon in Nabarangpur, and Telkoi and Champua in Keonjhar.

The low pressure area lay over Gangetic West Bengal and adjoining areas of Jharkhand and north Odisha in the morning, the bulletin stated.

Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning are likely over Gangetic West Bengal till Wednesday morning due to a low pressure area over the region, the IMD added.

World.title: Suvendu, Mamata spar over Annapurna Bhandar benefits in West Bengal
World.content:
The disbursement of cash to women under the West Bengal government’s Annapurna Bhandar scheme has given a handle to the Opposition parties to target the Suvendu Adhikari government.

Trinamool Congress chairperson Mamata Banerjee took the opportunity on Monday (August 24, 2026) to target the Bharatiya Janata Party government. “Before the election, the BJP did not discuss eligibility to receive the money. Will the BJP now decide who is eligible? Why are women not receiving money under the Annapurna scheme? Women are being given benefits based on caste and religion,” the former Chief Minister said.

Women in different parts of the State came out in protest last week, alleging that they have been denied benefits of ₹3000 per month under the scheme. Mr. Banerjee had launched a scheme to give cash to women in the State in 2021, and before the change of regime, the number of beneficiaries who were receiving the benefits of ₹1500 per month had climbed up to 2.2 crore.

On Monday (August 24, 2026), Ms. Banerjee assured women who have been denied benefits that she will stand by them. “Take down the names of those who are being deprived of Lakshmir Bhandar and Annapurna Yojana benefits. They will be contacted. I was with you, I am with you, and I will remain with you,” the Trinamool Congress chairperson said.

Alleging that the BJP government has denied her permission to hold public meetings, Ms. Banerjee also added that those who think she will retire from politics simply because of permission being denied permission are mistaken. “Our fight will not stop until the BJP itself is forced into political retirement,” she said.

Hours later Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that 1.45 crore beneficiaries have been disbursed with Annapurna Yojana funds. The Chief Minister tried to defend the fact that beneficiaries of Annapurna Bhandar are being scrutinised and said that if the scheme was universal, then why was it promised to women between 25 and 60 years of age during the Trinamool Congress regime.

Mr. Adhikari refuted allegations of Muslim being denied benefits under the scheme and said that about 19.20 lakh Muslims have got benefits under the scheme. “ Those eligible, whether Hindu or Muslim, Trinamool or BJP, have received the benefits,” the Chief Minister said. Mr. Adhikari said that a portal has been opened where people can lodge complaints for denial of benefits and also complain if anyone who is non-deserving is getting benefits of the scheme.

The Bhabanipur MLA, who had defeated the former Chief Minister on two occasions in 2026 and 2021, took a swipe at Ms. Banerjee who has been going live on social media rather than holding press conferences.

“Stay on Facebook, we will make arrangements so that she cannot go out on the streets,” Mr. Adhikari said.

World.title: Congress targets Modi government on price rise, 'ravaging’ the pathway from education to employment
World.content:
The Congress on Monday (August 24, 2026) targeted the Narendra Modi government over unemployment and price rise, with party president Mallikarjun Kharge accusing the government of “completely ravaging” young India’s entire pathway from education to employment.

Mr. Kharge cited a recent NITI Aayog report estimating that 8.7 crore Indians aged 15 to 29 years are neither studying, working or receiving training. Youth unemployment stood at 15.6%, rising to 19.5% among young women, he said, citing the Periodic Labour Force Survey for July 2026.

“Where are the jobs after graduation?” Mr. Kharge asked in a post on social media platform X, pointing out that graduates account for 67% of unemployed Indians aged 20 to 29 years. He also questioned the promise of creating two crore jobs every year, saying that, by that calculation, 24 crore jobs should have been created in 12 years.

Mr. Kharge alleged that lakhs of government posts remained vacant, while secure employment was increasingly being replaced by contractual and part-time work. “Expensive and inadequate education, paper leaks, delayed recruitment, a widening skills gap, and disappearing quality jobs have put the future of an entire generation at risk,” Mr. Kharge said.

“You, Modi ji, promised to achieve what previous governments could not do in 70 years! You have certainly delivered on that boast: an Education system that costs more, infested with RSS (Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh), examinations young Indians cannot trust, and degrees that increasingly come without jobs,” the Congress chief said.

The NITI Aayog report, Reimagining Skilling for Viksit Bharat@2047, based on data from the 78th round of the National Sample Survey conducted in 2021, has called for subsidised training programmes to encourage self-employment, and align skills with local demand and emerging sectors.

The Congress also attacked the government over the rising prices of essential commodities. The party’s communications chief Jairam Ramesh cited a media report on a sharp rise in onion prices, saying prices in Nashik had increased by around 76% in a month, while wholesale rates had doubled in some States.

“After sugar, now onions too are slipping out of the common man’s reach,” Mr. Ramesh said on X. The government’s buffer stock was empty, he claimed, adding that the rising prices of milk, oil, fruits, and other essential commodities were adding to the burden on households.

“The Modi government, which claims to have ushered in achchedin (good days), should explain how the poor and middle class were expected to make ends meet,” Mr. Ramesh said.

World.title: As many as 23,000 certificates issued under CAA, 2.3 lakh applications made says WB CM
World.content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday (August 24, 2026) said that 23,000 certificates under the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA), 2019 have been distributed out of the 2.30 lakh applications that have been made.

“Through the district magistrates, we will complete the hearings and grant the certificates. Now it is up to us to give certificates,” Mr. Adhikari said. The Chief Minister said that about 2.07 lakh applications are pending with the State government. He also urged people who have to come to India after facing religious persecution to apply to the State government for CAA certificates.

A few days ago, the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) transferred the processing of pending citizenship applications under the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA), 2019, from Empowered Committees to District Collectors in eight States and Union Territories.

During the campaign for the West Bengal Assembly elections 2026 Prime Minister Narendra Modi promised to fast-track and accelerate the implementation of the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) to grant legal citizenship rights to refugee communities like the Matuas and Namasudras.

Speaking to media persons at the State Secretariat, the Chief Minister said that the State’s Governor, R.N. Ravi, has given his nod for the new Act enabling the arrest of those attacking police, cost recovery for public property damage, and a notification was issued in this regard during the day.

Mr. Adhikari was referring to the West Bengal Maintenance of Public Order (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which imposes a payment of compensation on persons committing offences such as causing damage to public or private property. Another Bill passed by the State Assembly, the West Bengal Public Safety and Control of Anti-Social Activities Bill, 2026, which empowers the government to detain a person for 12 months is awaiting the nod of the President.

World.title: CJP calls for September 5 march from India Gate, accuses Centre of reneging on promises
World.content:
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has announced a march in Delhi on September 5, over the Centre’s alleged failure to honour the promises made during the July agitation.

In a statement posted on X, the CJP condemned the Union Government’s failure to honour the commitments made to India’s youth on July 25, particularly those concerning the withdrawal of FIRs against students and protesters.

“With the Government continuing to delay and avoid fulfilling its assurances, the CJP National Working Committee has decided to resume peaceful mobilisation,” it said in the statement.

Scheduled to take place on Teachers' Day, the march will start at India Gate and head toward the Delhi Police Headquarters, according to a statement from the CJP.

PRESS STATEMENT (Aug 24, 2026)



The Cockroach Janta Party strongly condemns the Union Government's failure to honour the commitments made to India's youth on July 25, particularly those concerning the withdrawal of FIRs against students and protesters.



With the Government… pic.twitter.com/YlmJJiYlqc — Cockroach Janta Party - CJP (@Cockroachisback) August 24, 2026

"We have not received any request letter so far. If we receive any request, we will review it accordingly," a police source said.

Along with the families of deceased NEET victims and victims of police brutality, the CJP will hold a peaceful youth march from India Gate to Delhi Police headquarters.

“The Government must honour its word. Our patience must not be mistaken for weakness,” it added.

It said the march would be led by families of students who died by suicide following the cancellation of the NEET exam and the subsequent re-test, and those who were allegedly subjected to police excesses during the July agitation.

The decision was taken at a meeting of the CJP National Working Committee on Monday (August 24, 2026), a month after the outfit called off its agitation following negotiations with the Centre.

(With inputs from PTI)

World.title: Uproar after Allahabad High Court refer Divisional Commissioner's conduct for criminal contempt
World.content:
Uproar took place on Monday (August 24, 2026) after Devipatan Divisional Commissioner Durga Shakti Nagpal allegedly attempted to influence a Civil Judge (Senior Division), Shabina Khan, in Gonda.

She is handling a civil suit, with social activists demanding a high-level investigation by the State government, and the Allahabad High Court referred the conduct to the court dealing with criminal contempt matters on August 21.

In the matter, the Civil Judge, Gonda, in a letter to the District Judge, said she received repeated calls while on leave on July 15, 2026 from a number linked to the Commissioner’s office.

Later, she said she got a call from Commissioner Durga Shakti Nagpal, who wanted to discuss the pending suit and asked pointed questions about how long she intended to stay on leave. The judge said the calls and the tone used amounted to interference.

In the matter, Allahabad High Court Justice Syed Qamar Hasan Rizvi on Friday (August 21, 2026) held that the allegations of pressure on the judicial officer could not simply be ignored and directed that the matter be placed before the appropriate bench dealing with criminal contempt.

Justice Rizvi noted that the District Judge, Gonda, had already transferred the suit to another equivalent court on 9 August 2026, so the transfer plea had lost its purpose. But held that the tone of the alleged conversation showed the judge was being pressured, and that courts cannot look away at insulting language used against a Presiding Officer. The Court directed that the matter be placed before the appropriate contempt bench after seeking directions from the Chief Justice or the Senior Judge.

Lucknow-based social activist Amitabh Thakur called for an independent, high-level inquiry into the matter and demanded that the Chief Secretary of U.P. immediately transfer Durga Shakti Nagpal from the Devipatan (Gonda) Division.

“I have sent a letter to the Chief Secretary of Uttar Pradesh demanding the transfer of Gonda (Devipatan) Commissioner Durga Shakti Nagpal and an independent high-level inquiry into the entire matter in light of an order passed by the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court on Friday (August 21, 2026), Mr. Thakur told The Hindu.

“The telephonic conversation between Gonda’s Civil Judge (Senior Division) and the Divisional Commissioner was, prima facie an attempt to influence a judicial officer, in accordance with the order of the High Court. I demanded that the Chief Secretary immediately transfer Durga Shakti Nagpal from Gonda Division and constitute an independent high-level administrative inquiry into the telephonic conversation with the judicial officer and the events that followed,” he added.

Mr. Thakur has also demanded that clear protocols and necessary administrative instructions be issued regarding executive officials contacting judicial officers in connection with pending judicial cases.

The Divisional Commissioner gave a different account of the events and said in a letter to the Administrative Judge, Gonda that she called only to check on the judge’s leave status since the case, pending nearly 30 years and involving land needed for her office building, required expediting, and that the judge reacted with anger and later declared in open court that she would not hear the matter further.

World.title: Row over U.P. IAS officer’s ‘bid’ to influence civil judge deepens as HC takes serious exception
World.content:
The controversy surrounding allegations that senior IAS officer and Devipatan Divisional Commissioner Durga Shakti Nagpal attempted to exert pressure on a civil judge intensified on Monday, with civil society members demanding a high-level probe by the Uttar Pradesh government.

The demand comes after the Allahabad High Court’s Lucknow Bench on Friday took serious exception to the allegation.

The Gonda civil judge, in a letter to the district judge, earlier alleged that she received repeated phone calls while on leave on July 15 from a number linked to the Devipatan Division Commissioner’s office, headquartered in Gonda. According to her, Ms. Nagpal, who wanted to discuss a long-pending land dispute, asked pointed questions about how long the judge intended to stay on leave. She also said the “phone calls and the tone used amounted to interference”.

The High Court observed that the pressure prima facie exerted by Ms. Nagpal “struck at the independence of the judiciary and obstructed the administration of justice”.

Ms. Nagpal, however, said she had not tried to discuss the merits of the case and had only sought to know when the judge would resume hearing the matter.

Justice Syed Qamar Hasan Rizvi held that the allegations could not simply be ignored, and directed that the matter be placed before the appropriate Bench dealing with criminal contempt. Justice Rizvi noted that the tone of the alleged conversation showed the judge was being pressured. The court directed that the matter be placed before the appropriate Bench after seeking directions from the Chief Justice or the senior judge.

“I have sent a letter to the Chief Secretary demanding the transfer of Durga Shakti Nagpal and an independent inquiry,” activist Amitabh Thakur said. He has also demanded clear protocols to be issued regarding officials contacting judicial officers over pending cases.

World.title: CDF Munir vows continued efforts to stabilise region in meeting with Iran’s Ghalibaf
World.content:
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir met Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf in Tehran on Monday during his visit to the Iranian capital, according to Iranian state broadcaster Press TV.

The CDF and interior minister reached Tehran earlier today, Iranian media reported, after Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) described the visit “as part of Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and stability”.

According to the Iranian broadcaster, Ghalibaf reaffirmed Tehran’s commitment to upholding the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, while criticising the United States for failing to honour its commitments. He said this approach had “hindered regional stability and further eroded trust in Washington”.

Field Marshal Munir said Pakistan would continue its efforts to help restore stability in the region, Press TV reported.

Later, Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, expressed his distrust of Washington during a meeting with Field Marshal Munir, according to the Fars news agency.

“America must change its behaviour and take practical actions regarding the implementation of the conditions of the agreement,” Rezaei was quoted as saying by Fars.

Iranian news agency ISNA has also published photographs of a meeting between Field Marshal Munir and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.

Earlier today, CDF Munir and Naqvi met with Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni in Tehran, state media in Pakistan reported.

Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said that the visit undertaken by CDF Munir and Naqvi was taking place as bilateral ties between Islamabad and Tehran “reach one of their strongest stages”, state broadcaster IRIB reported.

Baqaei added that the Pakistani delegation’s visit was unrelated to the visit of Oman’s foreign minister, who is expected to arrive today. He noted that “both visits will address regional security issues”.

ISPR said CDF Munir will “focus on promoting efforts towards peaceful, lasting and comprehensive resolution of the conflict in the Middle East” during the visit.

Baqaei on Sunday said CDF Munir was expected to travel to Tehran to continue efforts to bring peace and security to the region.

He said CDF Munir would lead an official delegation and the “visit aims to strengthen bilateral cooperation between Iran and Pakistan and to continue Pakis­tan’s good offices in support of peace and security in the region”.

During the visit, CDF Munir would meet and hold talks with senior officials Iran, Baqaei added.

The United States and Israel triggered the Middle East war with a massive wave of strikes against Iran on February 28, triggering Iranian retaliation across the region.

An April 8 ceasefire ended nearly 40 days of intense bombardment, but control over the Strait of Hormuz soon emerged as a key flashpoint in the conflict.

Iran has controlled the vital energy conduit since the war began. Reopening the strait, vital for global oil and gas supplies, has become a US priority, but Tehran insists the waterway will remain closed until Washington lifts its naval blockade on Iranian ports, removes oil sanctions and unfreezes Iranian assets abroad.

Pakistan has played a key role in efforts to halt war between Iran and the United States, brokering a memorandum of understanding (MoU) in June, but peace negotiations currently appear stalled.

Last week, US President Donald Trump announced that Washington would ramp up economic pressure on Iran “on an unprecedented scale”.

Washington has urged other governments, including Beijing, to join efforts to further isolate Iran’s economy.

The US is expected to announce details related to the planned sanctions on Mondau, which ​US officials have ​said would be “ the ⁠toughest sanctions in history ” on Iran.

Additional input from AFP

World.title: Govt increases petrol price by Rs0.39, high-speed diesel by Rs2.40
World.content:
The government on Monday raised the price of petrol by Rs0.39 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.40 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs341.98 per litre while HSD will cost Rs370.69 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on August 25.

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Joint opposition announces strategy against economic crisis, political repression
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The joint opposition held its first parliamentary meeting at Parliament House on Monday and announced a collective strategy to address violence, the economic crisis and political repression.

The meeting was attended by opposition party leaders, including Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas Jafri, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and others.

Speaking at a press conference after the meeting, the JUI-F chief said opposition parties had agreed to play a joint role in parliament and stressed that collective strategies and actions would be pursued through mutual consultation.

He said it was not the time to divide the provinces, warning that such a move would only increase mistrust among the federating units.

“We completely agree that this is absolutely not the time to divide the provinces; neither is the environment conducive to it nor is there any prior preparation.”

“Dividing the provinces will increase unrest,” he said, claiming that the 18th Amendment had become a “thorn in the throat” of the establishment.

He said all opposition parties agreed that Pakistan, at the state level, could not afford the prevailing situation. “People are also on the streets in Kashmir,” he said, alleging that violence was being used instead of addressing public grievances.

Fazl also called for the release of prisoners and the creation of a positive political environment.

He described the day as a “blessed day” and said lawmakers sitting on the opposition benches had decided to act as a joint opposition.

“We are together today in view of the law and order situation in the country,” he said. “On one side, our land is red with blood, while on the other, our rulers are walking on red carpets during foreign tours.”

He said the deteriorating law and order situation was also severely affecting the national economy. Referring to Pakistan’s rivalry with India, he said the two countries often talked about war and competition, while India had now become the world’s fourth-largest economy. He also questioned Pakistan’s standing in international judicial rankings.

Addressing the press conference, Achakzai said the opposition’s unity was a positive development, adding that opposition members had reached an agreement despite the “suffocating atmosphere” in parliament.

“It is a day of happiness and facilitation,” he said, expressing hope that the alliance would play an important role in restoring Pakistan’s lost glory.

“Today, there is unrest and bloodshed across the country, with more than 100 people losing their lives every day, yet no one seems to be paying any attention.

“The Constitution clearly lays down the procedure for creating provinces. In contrast, creating provinces through an executive order, in the same way that districts are created, would amount to an attack on the foundations of Pakistan.

“We warn those forces that if you do so, you will not be able to stop the people of Pakistan, and everyone will take to the streets. Pakistan can no longer afford to tolerate such circumstances,” he asserted.

“The poor are crying out for food, people are worried about employment, children are being deprived of basic necessities, and the education system is being ruined,” he said.

Meanwhile, Abbas said the opposition’s unity during the month marking the birth of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was a good sign.

“We are cultivating enmities instead of friendships,” he alleged, adding that the lives of citizens were not secure.

He also alleged that the sanctity of the home and the privacy of families were being violated and said that the honour and dignity of citizens were not protected.

Referring to the condition of incarcerated PTI leader Dr Yasmin Rashid, he said her situation was known to everyone. He also claimed that the Supreme Court had ordered the transfer of PTI founder Imran Khan to Shifa International Hospital, but alleged that the law and judicial decisions were being ignored.

Barrister Gohar said leaders of opposition parties had met and agreed to remain united.

“All opposition parties will adopt a common position in parliament,” he said, adding that they would speak with one voice on law and order, inflation and Pakistan’s relations with other countries.

He said the PTI had assured the JUI-F that it would give it full support.

On the question of provincial restructuring, he said no constitutional amendment concerning the provinces could be made overnight, stressing the need for consultation and consensus.

World.title: PTI says ‘Form 47’ govt lacks mandate to reshape country's governance structure
World.content:
PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said on Monday that the incumbent “Form 47” government had no mandate to reshape the country’s governance structure, adding that the party would welcome anyone willing to ally with it “in principle” on the issue.

Speaking on Geo News programme ‘Capital Talk’, Raja said the recent discussions with Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam chief Fazlur Rehman at the latter’s residence were based “on principle”.

“We all agreed that whatever has happened to this country over the past four years was against everyone’s wishes and expectations. In terms of the rule of law and the Constitution, the country has fallen into a deep ditch,” the PTI secretary general said.

“At this point, if someone feels that we are not where we were expected to be four years ago, whatever the reason, we need to consider the current situation objectively. Anyone can join us in principle,” he added.

Raja cautioned against altering the country’s federal system, describing discussions about an overhaul of the country’s entire structure as “hazardous”.

“The Form 47 assembly has no mandate to revamp the country’s system or governance structures,” he reiterated.

The senior PTI leader said any party that agreed with the PTI “in principle” on these issues could ally with it.

“Any political party that wants to strengthen the system, liberate the judiciary and reject rule by force in Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Balochistan or elsewhere can join us,” he said.

“It does not matter what our past was. We are very clear about our principles and our goal. We will welcome anyone who can go with us to some extent. A party can also end its journey with us. We are not depending on anyone,” he added.

Regarding the PTI’s call for a long march on Sept 27, Raja said the party would not stop any political party from joining it and would welcome those that did.

“Decisions will be taken at party forums — the core and political committees. If a party expresses its willingness to join the march, we will assess its goals and purpose,” he said.

Last week, the JUI-F chief also held a meeting with National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas and other opposition leaders, announcing the formation of a “united opposition”.

During the meeting, the leaders agreed to continue “further consultations among opposition parties” and formulate a joint course of action.

Meanwhile, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, who is an ally of the government, also met with the opposition leaders and agreed to maintain contact and cooperate on legislative matters in the parliament.

World.title: Family, legal team of Imaan and Hadi voice concerns over medical facilities at Adiala jail
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The families and legal team of incarcerated lawyers and human rights activists Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chatta have voiced concerns over the medical facilities available at Adiala jail.

On January 24, rights lawyers Imaan and Hadi were sentenced by an Islamabad sessions court to a total of 17 years in jail on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca).

Following their convictions, which were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts , the couple challenged their convictions before the Islamabad High Court (IHC) on February 7.

In a statement issued on Monday, the family and legal team said they were satisfied with the weekly meetings with the couple at the jail. However, they said Imaan had been experiencing health issues for the past three weeks, raising concerns about the medical facilities available at the jail.

“Imaan had initially complained of heavy bleeding from her gums, but there was no dentist available to examine her at the jail. We arranged for medicine to be sent to her after consulting our dentist, but not all of it reached her,” the statement alleged.

The following week, Imaan also suffered from stomach problems, and medical attention remained inadequate, it added.

“Worse, a medicine, Zedron, meant primarily for cancer patients and which specifically states that it should not be given to women of childbearing age, was administered to her to stop her nausea and vomiting,” the statement claimed.

For the past week, the family and legal team said Imaan had been suffering from a serious chest infection.

“They conducted a blood test which showed a high white blood cell count, indicating an infection. She needs to undergo a chest X-ray, but the jail authorities have still not arranged one to determine the cause of the infection and rule out serious diseases such as tuberculosis,” they said.

They maintained that their concern was compounded by the alarming fact that inmates in the women’s section of Adiala jail who had been diagnosed with infectious diseases were not isolated but housed alongside other inmates, as well as children.

“The women’s medical facilities and the availability of doctors leave a lot to be desired,” they stated.

“This is a health crisis in the jail, and the well-being of prisoners is the responsibility of the state, which must not take it lightly,” the statement said.

They reiterated that all these health issues could be avoided if their applications for suspension of sentence were heard in a timely manner.

They urged the jail authorities and the government to arrange Imaan’s chest X-ray as soon as possible and provide adequate medical facilities, including dental care, to all women prisoners.

They emphasised that detainees with infectious diseases should be isolated or quarantined with dignity to protect other detainees; that specialist doctors and access to relevant medication should be provided to all detainees; and that the government should not oppose the applications for suspension of sentence filed by Imaan and Hadi, which are scheduled to be heard by the IHC on Sept 8, 2026.

World.title: Protest at Islamabad varsity turns ugly after clash between uniformed individual, students
World.content:
A security official is in custody and facing disciplinary action under military law following reports of a scuffle at Islamabad’s Sarhad University of Science and Information Technology (SUSIT), sources involved in the investigation said late Monday.

The individual allegedly discharged a weapon during a scuffle with protestors at the university’s Chattha Bakhtawar campus, where students had been agitating against the dismissal of a senior official and other varsity-related issues.

A video shared widely on social media of the incident shows a uniformed individual approaching a group of young men, who are reportedly SUSIT students. He is accompanied by a woman, who is said to be a university official.

The video showed the suspect hitting an individual with a stick and exchanging heated words with gathered protestors, following which a scuffle breaks out. An angry crowd surrounds the officer, and some individuals appear to assault him, following which he draws a pistol and points it at the crowd.

The woman accompanying him appears to try to stop him, but the man then points the weapon into the air and discharges it, at which several police officers approach and encircle him.

In a later video, a senior Islamabad police official can be seen addressing the students. The individual was escorted out of the university by police, the police officer says, assuring that he will be dealt with strictly and swiftly under the army’s disciplinary procedures.

“The Pakistan Army’s foremost priority is to maintain a strict system of discipline and ensure justice. Further action will be taken in light of the findings of the inquiry,” sources privy to the matter said.

No official statement has been issued by the police, security forces or university yet.

World.title: Trump administration moves to impose more than $100,000 fee for H-1B worker visas
World.content:
President Donald Trump’s administration on Monday released a proposed regulation to codify an unprecedented more than $100,000 fee on new H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers, that Trump first imposed last year but has been blocked by the courts.

The fee first imposed by Trump in a temporary proclamation last year vastly raises the cost of the visas that are heavily relied on in the tech, education and research sectors.

A federal judge in June ruled that the fee was illegal and blocked the Trump administration from collecting it. A Boston-based appeals court is reviewing that decision while a different court considers whether a judge in Washington, DC, properly rejected a challenge to the fee by a major business group.

Trump’s 2025 proclamation imposing the fee expires in September, one year after it was issued, but directed the US Department of Homeland Security to adopt regulations making it permanent.

The proposed $103,265 fee by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), posted online in the Federal Register on Monday to be formally published on Tuesday, kicks off a 30-day public comment period.

The rule could be finalised by the end of the year.
